items.evidence: GET of the entry URL gave HTTP 200, 69,228 bytes, text/html, no redirect; robots.txt on housedivided.dickinson.edu is HTTP 404 (no restrictions). Page title is Blog Divided, Post Topic, Beyond Gettysburg: Primary Sources for the Gettysburg Campaign; posted by Cooper Wingert, 11 June 2018, filed under Civil War, Lesson Plans, Letters and Diaries, Lists. Its text says he assembled digitized primary sources from the House Divided Project, the Dickinson College Archives, the Cumberland County Historical Society and his 2012 book on the Confederate approach on Harrisburg, grouped as skirmishes, the occupation of Carlisle (June 27-28), York and Wrightsville, the Sporting Hill fight (June 30), the shelling of Carlisle (July 1-2), then Union, Confederate and civilian sources. The article region has 70 links. Matching claim 'finding aid used to build Part IX': I normalized the primary URL of every Part IX entry (579-625, 47 entries) and compared with the post's links: 47 of 47 are links in the post, in the same order as the post's sections. Member links on the dickinson.edu hosts that I fetched: 13 distinct archives.dickinson.edu URLs return 404 after an http to https redirect (the site now serves a Page not found); the post's own PDF copies on housedivided.dickinson.edu (Underwood letter, young girl's pocket diary, Anna Fosdick recollection, Hanna Culver letter, Richmond Enquirer July 17, Donavin 1998) and the hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu pages all returned 200. For all 13 dead URLs the Wayback availability API gave a capture (2015 to 2023) and I fetched each: HTTP 200 and the capture's page title names the same item. The page has almost nothing on African Americans: only a related-articles sidebar entry and the Hillman slavery debate and an abolitionist remark in the text.
items.extraction_notes: Static WordPress HTML; the article body is between the Posted by line and the Related Articles heading. Treat it as a to-do list of campaign sources (Carlisle, York, Sporting Hill, Harrisburg defenses), not as text to ingest. Capture a Wayback snapshot (2025-10-08 exists) if its exact link set must be cited, because the post is edited over time. Perseus (one link, Schuricht diary) must not be fetched; two HathiTrust links and Google Books links are not checkable by us.
issues: Filed under Part X (African Americans) although its own description says it was the finding aid for Part IX; I verified the Part IX link, 47 of 47.

Many member links are dead or restricted: 13 distinct archives.dickinson.edu 404s (entries 580, 581, 582, 587, 588, 603, 607, 615, 616, 620, 621, 624, 625; all have matching Wayback captures, see systemic findings), plus Perseus (robots-disallowed) and HathiTrust (bot-blocked).
Campaign context only (occupation of Carlisle, York, Sporting Hill, the July 1-2 shelling of Carlisle); no source in it describes the three-day battle at Gettysburg itself.
A living page, so the link set changes; no licence; only a short introduction is the author's own text.

items.written: The diary entries are dated 1863-06-30 to 1863-07-06 (TEI date range and the page's day headings); the Valley page itself is a modern landing page. The pages do not say whether each entry was written the same day; the July 6 entry is a long polished narrative, so treat it as diary-form and write down that this is unverified against the manuscript.
items.rights_basis: Valley of the Shadow Copyright and Fair Use Statement (fetched): freely available for non-commercial research, teaching, scholarship and private study; some materials may still be under copyright; users responsible for their own use; cite the source. The site footer links to the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 licence (NC, so not an open licence for general reuse). The TEI source file of the diary (FD1007.xml, linked from the diary page) states copyright 1998 by the Rector and Visitors of the University of Virginia, names as source copy the 1982 University of Pittsburgh Press edition The Cormany Diaries: A Northern Family in the Civil War, edited by James C. Mohr (with an assistant editor), and has the encoding note: Used with permission from Published Source. So the transcription and its footnotes reproduce a modern copyrighted edition with permission, and a non-commercial licence on the host cannot extend to the publisher's rights.
items.evidence: GET of the entry URL gave HTTP 200, 157,089 bytes, text/html, no redirect; robots.txt HTTP 404. The browser title is Letters of the Cormany Family, The War Years, The Valley of the Shadow; the page heading is Samuel and Rachel Cormany (1863) in the Franklin County diaries section. Content: a biography (Rachel born Bowman in Canada in 1836, Samuel born 1838 and raised in Chambersburg, married November 1860 after meeting at Otterbein, returned to Chambersburg August 1862, Samuel enlisted as second lieutenant in the 16th Pennsylvania Cavalry in September 1862) and two excerpt blurbs: Samuel's diary of service in the 16th Pennsylvania Cavalry in the Gettysburg Campaign, late June to early July 1863 (rumors of battle, then the battle, then pursuit and a chance to see his wife), and Rachel's diary of panic and occupation in Chambersburg. The cards that open the diaries are rendered by the page's JavaScript (component ids FD1007 and FD1006), so the static HTML has no anchors to them; I did not render the page. I fetched the Samuel diary page https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/diaries/FD1007 (HTTP 200): title Franklin County, Diary of Samuel Cormany (1863); daily entries June 30 to July 6 with seven footnotes. Two concrete checks of the description: the July 1 entry has him at Hanover hearing cannonading and then musketry toward Gettysburg and a rumor of battle; the July 3 entry reports the heaviest cannonading he had ever heard, about 1:30 to 4 pm, with his squadron on the right of the line; footnote 7 confirms the 16th Pennsylvania pursued the retreating Confederates toward Chambersburg and the July 6 entry has him leaving the column to reach his wife and child. Cross-check against the OR order of battle (read in the Archive OCR, p. 167): the 16th Pennsylvania Cavalry (Lt. Col. John K. Robison) is listed in the Third Brigade (Col. J. Irvin Gregg), Second Division, Cavalry Corps, whereas the July 2 entry names the 2nd Brigade, 2nd Division; the diary's and the OR's brigade number disagree (cause not determined). The first pass said the Stuart explanation sits on the July 2 entry; in fact footnote 4 (Stuart's ride) is attached to the July 1 entry.
items.extraction_notes: Do not ingest. If the owner wants this diary linked, link the diary page FD1007 directly (this entry's page holds only a biography and two blurbs, not the diary text), cite as the Valley asks, and do not copy the footnotes (modern editorial text). Each Valley item carries a TEI source file that shows its source and copyright; read it before any other Valley diary or letter (Part XI) is treated as open.
issues: Rights: the transcription comes from a 1982 published edition and is used with permission, with UVA copyright 1998 and a non-commercial licence badge; not open, so link-out only regardless of whether the project is commercial.
The entry's page is a landing page, not the diary; the diary text is at the FD1007 page, which no list entry links to (entry 640 is Rachel's diary, FD1006).
Source of the transcription is not credited on the entry page but is in the TEI header (1982 Pitt Press edition), correcting the first pass.

Dating: diary entries are dated, but the pages do not say whether they were written each day; the OR order of battle puts the 16th Pennsylvania in the Third Brigade while the diary says the 2nd Brigade, so check any unit or time claim before use.
The editorial footnotes cite two modern books (1958, 1963) and are the editors' text, not Cormany's.

summary: Independent second verification of 8 entries (649, 650, 652, 580, 581, 582, 583, 603): all 8 get APPROVE, matching the first pass on verdict and rights tier for every entry (1 at A1: 652; 7 at A2). I differ on a few details. 581's description is inaccurate, not just imprecise. 650 carries a real battle narrative, so I rate its relevance higher. 603's PDF damage is quantified. Seven of the eight are hold-for-rights-review or blocked-for-transcription in practice. Method: my own polite fetches (honest User-Agent, 1.2 s per host, robots.txt read first, no browsers). Perseus article text was not fetched (robots.txt blocks it); I read the same article in the Internet Archive scan instead. Every byte count and sha256 I fetched that the first pass also reported matched exactly: IA OCR text 8467b13f..., Valley XML for 650 dea3d35a..., 580 PDF 19aed028..., 582 PDF bf38abdd.... Not verified: the content of the Perseus page; Isaac Harris's death date; whether the current Dickinson site holds the three Dickinson items elsewhere (its search is blocked by robots, and the one collection listing I could browse has none of them); manuscript-versus-transcript comparison, except one handwritten page of 581 that I viewed; the Davis/Dahlgren claim in entry 652.
systemic_findings: Provenance of the Dickinson entries: entries 580, 581, 582, 583 and 603 all come from one House Divided blog post, Beyond Gettysburg: Primary Sources for the Gettysburg Campaign, by Cooper Wingert, 11 June 2018 (https://housedivided.dickinson.edu/sites/blogdivided/2018/06/11/beyond-gettysburg-primary-sources-for-the-gettysburg-campaign/, fetched). The list copied that post's one-line glosses and its links. Its links to archives.dickinson.edu and the old UVA Valley URL are the same ones now dead or generic. The blog's gloss that Hillman debated officers about slavery became the list's wording; the post lumps Himes's letter and diary into one item, and the list split them.

Descriptions derived from blog glosses are unreliable: 581 does not describe the occupation or shelling of Carlisle (it is written from New Oxford and covers Hanover and Gettysburg), 582 is mostly not in Carlisle, 580 overstates slavery. A description should not be used for relevance classification without reading the document.

All four Dickinson Civil War Resources pages 404 on the current site, which no longer has that section. The one collection listing I could browse (MC 2000.1 Himes, 14 items; browsing is not blocked, site search is) has no Civil War items. I did not search the whole site. All matching copies found are Wayback captures; Wayback CDX returned 503 and ECONNREFUSED (Internet Archive temporarily offline) late in the session, so the capture lists for 582 and 603 are incomplete.

hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu serves a 600-second Crawl-delay and its robots.txt could not be read by the host's own TLS certificate for hd.dickinson.edu; I did not fetch it. The blog host housedivided.dickinson.edu has no robots.txt (404) and is fetchable.

The Valley of the Shadow (entries 649, 650, 583 and the rest of Part XI) is offered for non-commercial use only, with a CC BY-NC 4.0 link in every page footer and some materials possibly still under copyright; the original texts are 1863 and public domain, but the transcriptions are UVA's. One human decision on the non-commercial condition settles all Valley entries.

Perseus (www.perseus.tufts.edu) robots.txt allows only /hopper/grants, research, about, collections and index.html for all agents and names Anthropic crawlers explicitly; /hopper/text, the path SHSP articles use, is not allowed. SHSP vol. 28 is available from the Internet Archive scan southernhistoric2819sout (UF scan, 1900 imprint, out of copyright per its metadata); also found: a 1991 Broadfoot reprint (southernhistoric0028rabr, exclude) and a second 1900 scan (bwb_S0-DSF-019_28, not read).
Wayback PDFs are fragile: the Harris diary capture is cut at 1 MiB and unreadable by standard tools; the Himes letter PDF exists only in a 2024 capture under a different path from the 2015 item page.

Rights for the Dickinson items: underlying texts are old (authors died 1912, 1918, 1899, Harris unverified), but the host asserts all rights reserved over scans and transcripts and adds modern notes (Harris). Those items are approved only at A2 pending a human decision.

items.written: 1863-07-15 (Franklin Repository, weekly, Chambersburg; contents run from late June to 13 July 1863)
items.rights_basis: The underlying text is an 1863 American newspaper, so public domain on imprint year. The host adds terms. Valley of the Shadow /about/copyright (fetched, 200) says some materials may still be under copyright and that the site is freely available for non-commercial uses in research, teaching, scholarship and private study; users are responsible for their own use and must cite. The footer of the issue page, and of the other Valley pages I fetched, links to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/ (BY-NC, not an open licence for commercial reuse). The TEI header of this issue carries no rights statement, so the site-level terms apply. The transcription is a UVA/New American History product (first pass only). A human must decide whether the non-commercial condition is acceptable before any verbatim quote ships (ingest state hold:rights-review).
items.evidence: Fetched https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/newspapers/franklin-repository/1863/07/15 myself: 200, 384,777 bytes (complete; the earlier probe cache was truncated at 327,680), sha256 ac54242c56e4d566ff7c03d1d4be156b0451f6436e43b09b15c6ea73a8c83e99; title Franklin Repository: July 15, 1863; valley host robots.txt is 404 (no restrictions). Also fetched the TEI source, api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.15.xml: 141,258 bytes, sha256 71fcadc2f7a9af7d15992c2bb08b247a97d77500445556fee5dd620577c84f4c; weekly, Wednesday, 8 pages, 33 article divisions, 17 [illegible] markers, a single tagger 'Sally Henninger, 1st pass' (no second proofing pass recorded). Claim 1 (read in the text): page 1 column 1, headed THE INVASION!, reprints Lee's General Orders No. 72 dated 21 June 1863, Ewell's General Orders No. 49 of 22 June, Ewell's Chambersburg orders of 24 June, Lee's General Orders No. 73 of 27 June and Ewell's General Order No. 51 (court-martial results). Claim 2: the same article goes on to Confederate conduct around Chambersburg: the burning of Thaddeus Stevens's iron works, the killing of Mr. Strite near the Greencastle road by soldiers of Hill's corps, and a section titled Bombardment of Carlisle. Beyond the list description: page 2 column 1 (The Battle of Gettysburg) relays the Philadelphia Inquirer's description of 1 July and Richmond papers; page 4 has a Pennsylvania Reserves article and Meade/Lee notes; page 5 has Lee's retreat across the Potomac on 13 July.
items.extraction_notes: Segment by article division (each has page, column, summary, excerpt and 'Full Text of Article') from the page HTML or the TEI XML. Page 1 column 1 is one long compilation article that reprints Lee's and Ewell's orders; take the orders from the Official Records, not from this issue. Keep [illegible] markers (17) and do not fill them. Strip the Valley's summary, excerpt and names fields (modern editorial metadata). Check any quote against the page images ('Newspaper Images' on the page) because only a first-pass transcription exists. Cite as Franklin Repository (Chambersburg), 15 July 1863, p. N, col. N, via Valley of the Shadow.
issues: List description covers only page 1 column 1; the issue also prints second-hand battle reports (page 2), a Reserves article (page 4) and the retreat (page 5).
First-pass transcription only (17 illegible gaps, one tagger, no second pass recorded).
Valley terms are non-commercial only and the footer links CC BY-NC 4.0: one human rights decision is needed for the whole Valley part (Part XI).
A weekly assembled from reports and reprints during the days and weeks after the events; not a same-day source. The reprinted orders are secondary copies of OR documents.
Strongly Unionist editorial voice (visible in the Valley's own summaries of the leaders).

items.written: 1863-07-29 (Franklin Repository, weekly, Chambersburg); includes a letter datelined Gettysburg, 15 July 1863
items.rights_basis: Same basis as entry 649. The underlying 1863 newspaper text is public domain on imprint year. The host terms are non-commercial use, with a CC BY-NC 4.0 link in the footer of this page (confirmed in the HTML; the TEI header has no rights statement). Because of the non-commercial condition, a human must clear the site terms before verbatim quoting (hold:rights-review).
items.evidence: Fetched https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/newspapers/franklin-repository/1863/07/29: 200, 340,929 bytes, sha256 7566330e0d4d9d7f9e7f5a3e0b6b1c3a0e1f7c3e1a2b4d5c6e7f8091a2b3c4d5 is NOT claimed; the exact sha256 recorded by my client is 7566330e... (see the saved copy; first 8 hex digits 7566330e). I also fetched the TEI XML, api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.29.xml: 110,276 bytes, sha256 dea3d35a7da6faace329dff98c07c80204e61c0104e8db0ca43dd66cc7f0cdd3; 8 pages, 51 article divisions, 16 [illegible] markers, taggers 'Sally Henninger, 1st pass' and 'Susanna Michele Lee, 2nd pass, 12/22/98'. Claim 1: page 2 column 2 is headed Gen. S. Wiley Crawford and the Pennsylvania Reserves, 'Correspondence of the Franklin Repository, Gettysburg, July 15, 1863'. It relays a sketch from an unnamed gentleman who says he saw it all: the Reserves reached the field at 11 a.m. on Thursday 2 July and went in with the Fifth Corps on the left; the sketch carries on into Friday 3 July. Claim 2: page 8 column 4 lists three hospitals for the wounded in Chambersburg (Academy hospital under Dr. Senseny, Town Hall under Dr. Richards, School House for wounded rebels under Confederate Assistant Surgeon Gamble); page 8 column 2 reports Col. Benjamin F. Carter, 4th Texas, dead of Gettysburg wounds at the Academy hospital. Also page 2 column 1 (The Gettysburg Battlefield) is a visitor's narrative from the Tuesday after the fight. The Valley summary calls the general 'Gen. S. Wylie'.
items.extraction_notes: Segment by article division (51). The Reserves piece and the battlefield visit are the long narrative items; hospital and personal items are one-paragraph local news. Cite the Repository correspondent as the author of the datelined letter and name the sketch as an unnamed eyewitness's account relayed by him. Keep [illegible] markers (16). Strip the Valley's summary, excerpt and name-index fields. The correct general is Samuel Wylie Crawford; do not copy the Valley summary's 'Wylie' as a name.
issues: The Reserves sketch is an anonymous witness account relayed by a correspondent, datelined 15 July, not a signed eyewitness report.
Valley summary misnames the general (Wylie for Samuel Wylie Crawford); metadata error.
Hospital and wounded items are short local news on page 8, not a main article.
16 [illegible] markers.
Non-commercial Valley terms and the CC BY-NC link: hold for rights review.

items.written: 1900 (Southern Historical Society Papers vol. 28, Richmond, Jan-Dec 1900); abstracts of documents dated from late March to 28 June 1863
items.rights_basis: Imprint read from the title page in the Internet Archive scan I fetched (southernhistoric2819sout): Volume XXVIII, Richmond, Va., Published by the Society, 1900, printed by Wm. Ellis Jones. IA metadata: University of Florida scan, 2015, 408 images, possible-copyright-status 'Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright'. A US imprint before 1931 is public domain. The abstracted documents are US Government works. Do not use the 1991 Broadfoot reprint (southernhistoric0028rabr), which my IA search also returned.
items.evidence: Perseus link NOT fetched. I read https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/robots.txt (200): User-agent: * allows only /hopper/grants, /hopper/research, /hopper/about, /hopper/collections and /hopper/index.html, then Disallow: /. The /hopper/text path in the listed URL is not allowed, and the file names Anthropic crawlers specifically. I evaluated our User-Agent against it with the QC library: not allowed. Instead I used IA search (advancedsearch) to find the 1900 volume and fetched archive.org/metadata/southernhistoric2819sout (200; title 'Southern Historical Society papers', v.28(1900), 408 images) and its OCR djvu.txt (1,077,008 bytes, sha256 8467b13f01c1608d4fc32b044963722889ee5636fba7655097402b18fc80ebef) plus page_numbers.json (leaf 162 is printed p. 148, leaf 170 is p. 156). The volume contents list item XVII: The Correspondence of General R. E. Lee, Chancellorsville to Gettysburg, March to August 1863, by Col. Wm. H. Palmer, p. 148; the next article, on Grady, starts p. 156, so the article is pp. 148-155. Claim 1: the article is a table of abstracts of OR letters from March to June 1863 under OR vol. XXV pt. II and vol. XXVII pt. III headings; the correspondents include Lee, Seddon, Davis, Cooper, S. Jones, A. P. Hill, Stuart, Pickett, Jenkins and D. H. Hill, not only Lee to Davis. Lee-to-Davis items from June include 2, 9, 23 and 25 June (Williamsport). Claim 2: the 28 June Davis letter appears only in a closing note, saying it was entrusted to a courier captured by Capt. Dahlgren of Meade's staff. It is not one of the abstract entries, and I did not check that claim against the OR. The editor's note names Palmer as formerly chief of staff to A. P. Hill.
items.extraction_notes: Use the Internet Archive scan, never Perseus. The IA OCR has no page breaks, so take printed page numbers from the running heads (148 to 155); the OCR garbles the OR page citations and years (the digits come out as letters and symbols), so no citation may be copied from the OCR. This is a retrospective 1900 compilation with an advocacy frame; label it as such and quote the actual documents from the OR rather than these abstracts. Cite as William H. Palmer, 'The Correspondence of Gen. Robt. E. Lee', SHSP 28 (1900): 148-155.
issues: The listed Perseus URL cannot be fetched by a program (robots.txt); I could not confirm that chapter 1.16 is this article.
Description partly inaccurate: the table covers late March to June 1863, many correspondents, not only June dispatches to Davis; the 28 June Davis letter is an end note.
Author (Col. William H. Palmer) and pages (148-155) are missing from the entry.
Retrospective (1900) and partisan: secondary, not a primary source; frames the abstracts to show Lee thwarted.
OCR page references and dates are unreliable.
1991 reprint (southernhistoric0028rabr) is not allowable; a second 1900 scan, bwb_S0-DSF-019_28, exists and was not read.
Davis letter / Dahlgren statement in the article not checked against the OR.

items.written: Published 1863-07-18 in The Methodist (New York), about events 27 June to 2 July 1863 in Carlisle; date comes from the catalogue, not from the clipping
items.rights_basis: Underlying work: an 1863 periodical article by Samuel Dickinson Hillman, who died in December 1912 per the Dickinson encyclopedia entry I fetched. A published pre-1931 work is public domain, and a scan of a printed page adds no new text. Weaknesses: the imprint date is taken from the host catalogue, not read from the clipping (the visible masthead shows The Methodist, New-York, without a date). The host's item page says it is copyright by Archives and Special Collections at Dickinson College, all rights reserved, with no reuse licence. The PDF is image-only, so any quotable text would be our own transcription.
items.evidence: Listed URL re-fetched: http 301 to https, then 404 (25,366 bytes, 'Page not found'); the Dickinson robots.txt allows these paths. The current Dickinson site has no Civil War Resources section. Wayback capture 20231207203932 of the listed page (200, 26,514 bytes) shows the item: 'The Methodist, A Few Days Under Rebel Rule', 11 pages, date July 18 1863, MC 2000.9 B1 F3, gift of Dr. Theodore M. Johnson, copyright notice 'Archives and Special Collections at Dickinson College, All rights reserved'. Its PDF resolved to capture 20240620182759: 3,555,300 bytes, sha256 19aed028b2b7dfa6d5f0322d5f1e29a44f1247490d563b50aec3b9ef95223174; 11 pages: a cover with text, nine thin column crops and one full-clipping image, with no text layer. I rendered and read the images. Claim 1: the byline reads By Prof. S. D. Hillman, Carlisle, and the title A Few Days under Rebel Rule; the first section is the rebel entrance into Carlisle on Saturday (27 June) around 10 a.m. Claim 2: sections include Discussion with Rebel Officers (with Majors Pendleton of Ewell's staff and Allen), Talk of the Rebel Chaplain, Arrival of the Union Army, The Bombardment of Carlisle and Wantonness of the Rebel Attack (shelling by Fitzhugh Lee's force about 3 a.m. Thursday 2 July). Slavery enters through the officers' demand for all the slave states and their complaint about the freeing of their slaves, and Hillman calls it a slaveholders' war, but the main argument is over who is winning and the divine favor claimed. Author data: Hillman (1825-1912), Dickinson Class of 1850, professor of mathematics and astronomy from 1860 (Dickinson encyclopedia entry fetched).
items.extraction_notes: Image-only, so the path is manual transcription or OCR of printed type (it reads cleanly); a second person should check it against the images. Hillman, A Few Days Under Rebel Rule, The Methodist (New York), 18 July 1863 (clipping MC 2000.9 B1 F3, Dickinson College Archives). Period racial terms occur in the text.

items.written: 1863-10-02 (written at New Oxford, Adams County, Pa.), about events from about 25 June to early July 1863
items.rights_basis: Unpublished 1863 manuscript letter by Charles Francis Himes, who died in December 1918 per the Dickinson encyclopedia entry I fetched, so its US copyright term has run out. The host item page (Wayback capture) states copyright by the Dickinson College Archives and all rights reserved; the typed transcript included in the PDF is the host's work. The listed link is dead and the PDF exists only in a 2024 capture. Needs a human rights review before quoting.
items.evidence: Listed URL (path /civil-war/...): http 301 to https, then 404 (25,346 bytes). Wayback CDX for the listed path shows a 2015 capture (200), and for /civil-war-resources/... captures 2019-2024. I fetched capture 20240803064910 of /civil-war-resources/letter-charles-f-himes-ogden-n-rood (200, 26,901 bytes): 'Letter from Charles F. Himes to Ogden N. Rood', 13 pages, date October 2 1863, MC 2000.1 B10 F10, 'Transcript included', gift of Mary Himes Vale and Sarah Vale Rush. Its PDF resolved to capture 20240703042213: 5,068,054 bytes, sha256 ebacbeef0a366cbe42524a9b0d0987a8c57d585bcc8cd05fcfc425724f56807f; 13 pages = cover, 6 handwritten sheets (images; the text layer is garbage) and 6 typed transcript pages (noisy but readable text layer). I read the transcript and viewed sheet 1 (heading New Oxford Adams Co., Oct 2nd 1863, Dear Rood). Findings against the list description: (a) it is not a description of the occupation or shelling of Carlisle. Himes was at Carlisle for Commencement about 25 June, saw the militia and two New York regiments man defences a mile west of town, and left for home before the Confederates arrived; (b) the Rebels he describes pass through New Oxford (Gordon's brigade), he watches the cavalry fight at Hanover on Tuesday 30 June, walks to Gettysburg on Wednesday 1 July (the Rebels have taken the town and turn him away), is sent off again on Thursday 2 July, and encloses a fern from Round Top. Dickinson encyclopedia: in 1863 Himes was Dickinson Class of 1855 and had been professor at Troy University (not yet a Dickinson professor), and he attended the New Oxford institute.
items.extraction_notes: Two layers: six sheets of handwriting (image only) and a typed transcript (text layer with OCR noise: broken words such as 't hat', stray symbols, dropped letters, especially on transcript page 2). Use the typed transcript as the text source after checking each quote against the transcript image, and against the handwriting where possible. Cite as Charles F. Himes to Ogden N. Rood, New Oxford, Pa., 2 Oct 1863, MC 2000.1 B10 F10, Dickinson College Archives.

Written three months later (2 Oct 1863), so retrospective rather than same-day.
Entry calls him a Carlisle civilian; he lived at New Oxford and was not yet a Dickinson professor.
Transcript text layer is noisy; handwriting is image-only.

items.written: Diary entries 1863-06-23 to 1863-07-03 (typed transcript, partial; the transcript stops mid-entry on 3 July)
items.rights_basis: Unpublished 1863 diary of Charles Francis Himes (died December 1918 per the Dickinson encyclopedia entry I fetched), so the term has run out. The host item page states copyright by the Dickinson College Archives, all rights reserved. The only text is the host's typed partial transcript; the manuscript is not shown. Human rights review needed.
items.evidence: Listed URL: http 301 to https, then 404 (25,359 bytes). Wayback capture 20240302072813 of the item page (200, 27,488 bytes): 'Pocket Diary of Charles F. Himes', 3 pages, date 1863, MC 2000.1 B16 F2, 'Partial transcript included; a complete transcript for this diary is not yet available'. Its PDF resolved to capture 20240620182659: 968,550 bytes, sha256 bf38abddc70019d8a35e234a462a1b761ed1d4c8fa764e3720045564fb52744e; 3 pages (cover plus 2 typed transcript pages with a text layer). I rendered page 2 and read all text. Claim 1: entries start Tuesday 23 June (drove to Carlisle, Rebels at Shippensburg, Belles Lettres exhibition) and Thursday 25 June (degrees conferred, walked to the fortifications, left for home as Rebels were within 4 miles). Claim 2: from 27 June the entries are at New Oxford (about 3,000 infantry of Gordon's brigade, Early's division, Ewell's corps pass through and burn a railroad bridge and warehouse), then Hanover on Tuesday 30 June (cannonading), and on 1-3 July on the road toward Gettysburg (Confederate pickets turn him back; ambulances carrying off dead and wounded; heavy firing on 3 July). So the Confederate presence in the diary is at New Oxford, Hanover and the Gettysburg road, not in Carlisle, and nothing is said of the shelling.
items.extraction_notes: The PDF is a typed transcript image with a clean text layer (pdf-text works). Cite as Charles F. Himes pocket diary 1863, MC 2000.1 B16 F2, Dickinson College Archives, partial transcript. No manuscript images online, so quotes cannot be checked against the handwriting.

items.written: 1863-06-28 (letter written at Carlisle, Pa., Headquarters Second Corps A.N.V.)
items.rights_basis: Underlying work: a private 1863 letter by Jedediah Hotchkiss (1828-1899), so its US term has run out. The host adds claims: the Valley TEI header (api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/papers/A4042.xml, 10,357 bytes, sha256 6ebf1959bfe78e3e4c70bcb077e8c8f6fd5d15b52a2dd62606b4565df7c1d102) says text copyright 2001 by the Rector and Visitors of the University of Virginia and 'Used with permission from Library of Congress' (source copy: Hotchkiss Collection, Reel 4, LC). Site terms are non-commercial use and the footer links CC BY-NC 4.0. The Modern Spelling version is an editorial layer. A human must decide whether the non-commercial terms are acceptable.
items.evidence: Listed URL http://valley.lib.virginia.edu/papers/A4042: two 301s (to https://valley.lib.virginia.edu/papers/A4042, then to https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/) and a 200 generic home page: a dead link in disguise. https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/papers/A4042 redirects (302) to https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/letters/A4042: 200, 166,712 bytes, 'Augusta County: Jedediah Hotchkiss to Sara A. Hotchkiss, June 28, 1863', with Original and Modern Spelling versions. Wayback capture 20240707204400 of the old URL (200, 8,591 bytes) shows the same letter text with no HTML title element, which explains the probe's 'title unclear'. Claim 1: the letter is headed Hd. Qrs. 2nd Corps A.N.V., Carlisle Pa., 28 June 1863, and says the army reached Carlisle the previous day, quartered troops at the US Barracks and in Dickinson College's yard, and made requisitions on the town for supplies and medicines. Hotchkiss, Carlisle, 28 June 1863, Hotchkiss Collection, LC, via Valley of the Shadow (letters/A4042).

Any diarist of 1863 would have been dead before 1955, so the unpublished-work term ended in 2002, but I did not confirm his death date. The host item page states copyright by the Dickinson College Archives, all rights reserved. The text is a transcript with modern editorial notes added by the host (16 blocks starting with '>'); those notes are host-owned and must not be quoted as the diarist's words. The full transcript is at the US Army Heritage and Education Center per the catalogue.
items.evidence: Listed URL: http 301 to https, then 404 (25,372 bytes). Wayback capture 20231210113055 of the item page (200, 26,828 bytes): 'Isaac Harris Diary, U.S. Sanitary Commission', 16 pages, June 12 - July 18, 1863, I-BaldwinC-1998-1; 'a transcript of a portion'; gift of Caroline Harris Baldwin. Its PDF link resolved to capture 20220518060218: exactly 1,048,576 bytes, sha256 8f94b72c9631cb7382e64ba1e87faf88a76d108444670240981226f27f222ee0. It is truncated: the linearization dictionary says the full file is 1,063,700 bytes, the xref table and trailer are missing, and PyMuPDF, pdftotext and pypdf all fail to open it. I recovered the text by decoding the Flate page content streams (15 scanned pages plus a cover; the last page image is only partly present, 31,337 of 36,406 stream bytes). The text covers every day from Friday 12 June to Saturday 18 July. Claim 1: on Wednesday 1 July at Carlisle he describes Fitzhugh Lee's demand to surrender, the shelling of the main street, and taking shelter under the lee of the jail wall with Gowan and Smith. Claim 2: on Tuesday 7 July he walks to the hospital at Dickinson College, talks with Dr. Tomlinson, learns what supplies were needed and hauls stores; by 9-10 July he visits hospitals including about 70 Rebel patients under a Confederate surgeon.
items.extraction_notes: Text path: decode the page content streams of the truncated PDF (custom script; ordinary readers fail) or find a complete capture. Segment one passage per dated entry (about 37). The diary uses racial slurs in the diarist's own words. Cite as Isaac Harris diary, 12 June - 18 July 1863, Dickinson College Archives (I-BaldwinC-1998-1), partial transcript.

summary: Independent second verification of 8 entries (607, 612, 615, 616, 649, 650, 652, 580). Every verdict was derived from my own fetches (Wayback captures, the live Dickinson, Valley of the Shadow and Notre Dame hosts, the Internet Archive scan of SHSP vol. 28). I did not fetch Perseus, hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu (robots Crawl-delay 600, so skipped), HathiTrust or eHistory, and I launched no browser. Result: APPROVE 616, 649, 650, 652, 580; APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY 607, 612, 615. Compared afterwards with the first pass, all 8 verdicts and the tiers for 615 (unknown) and 652 (A1) are the same. Differences in detail: (1) the July Stayman PDF capture I fetched is complete (6 pages, 3,108,759 bytes), while the Wayback copy of the August PDF is cut off at exactly 1,048,576 bytes and cannot be opened, but the August letter is live and complete on the new Dickinson host (2,062,386 bytes); (2) for Notre Dame I could not confirm that the new host 'shows images only': the legacy path returns an S3 AccessDenied (403) XML and the 'Manuscripts of the American Civil War' link on the new digital index points to a page that says the site is offline; (3) I mark the Franklin Repository issues as only partly transcribed (7 of 33 and 6 of 50 items have a full-text block); (4) the Hillman 'debates about slavery' wording is a mild overstatement. Limits: I did not read all of the Hillman, Sullivan or Stayman texts (selected passages, with at least two concrete claims checked per entry), I could not open the Perseus page, and 'professor' for Stayman rests only on a search-result snippet that I did not confirm on a fetched page. Wayback and its CDX endpoint were intermittently offline (ECONNREFUSED and 503 'Temporarily Offline'); I backed off and retried.
systemic_findings: Wayback availability: the Wayback Machine and its CDX endpoint were intermittently offline during the run (ECONNREFUSED, then an HTTP 503 'Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline' page). The polite client caches failures, so a retry needs a refresh after a wait of about a minute; calls worked again after backing off. Use raw captures (the 'id_' form) for HTML and PDFs.

A Wayback PDF capture can be silently truncated: the capture of the Stayman August letter PDF (20240624092903) stops at exactly 1,048,576 bytes and does not open (linearized header declares 2,062,461). Check byte length against the PDF's own declared length, and look for a live copy.

Dickinson Archives has moved some Civil War documents to a new host layout: /document-descriptions/<slug>, /archives-people/<slug>, PDFs at /sites/default/files/files_document/<id>_2.pdf. The Stayman August letter is live there (page and complete PDF), but for the Hillman article, the Cumberland Valley broadside and the Sullivan pamphlet, the people page or guessed slugs gave no live copy (404), so Wayback remains the only source found for them. Other batches should try the live /archives-people/<name> pages before relying on Wayback. Not exhaustive: I did not crawl the new site's listings.

Dickinson's Civil War PDFs are mixed: transcript-bearing items (Stayman) have a typed transcript page with a text layer; the 1863 prints and clippings (Hillman article, broadside) are image-only with no or garbled OCR (manual transcription); the 1933 Sullivan pamphlet has a usable but error-prone OCR layer.

Notre Dame: the legacy rarebooks.nd.edu paths redirect (301) to the new home page, and the new host's own 'Manuscripts of the American Civil War' links point to a notice that the site is offline. The legacy paths on the new host return an S3-style AccessDenied (403), which I treated as 'not present', not as a bot block. The only readable copies are Wayback captures; the transcriptions carry a Notre Dame copyright notice with no licence.

Perseus (robots Disallow: /) was not fetched; the same SHSP article was verified in the Internet Archive scan (OCR text 1,077,008 bytes plus page-number map). The hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu host states Crawl-delay: 600 and Disallow: /search/, so I did not crawl it; claims that depend on it (Stayman being a professor) stay unconfirmed.

Valley of the Shadow (valley.newamericanhistory.org): robots 404 on the main host, empty Disallow on the api host; the footer links CC BY-NC 4.0 and the Copyright and Fair Use Statement allows non-commercial uses and warns some materials may still be under copyright. Newspaper pages are only partly transcribed (7 of 33 and 6 of 50 items in the two issues checked); project summaries, excerpts and names are not the newspaper's words. TEI XML is available per issue on the api host, which makes extraction easy but does not change the rights position.

Search-engine summaries returned by WebSearch were treated only as leads for URLs; every URL used was fetched directly. Their statements (for example Stayman's chair, or 'beyond Gettysburg' collection claims) were not used as evidence unless I confirmed them on a fetched page.

items.written: 1863-08-07 (near Orange Court House, Va.)
items.rights_basis: Unpublished 1863 letter by an author who died 9 Nov 1863, so public domain by date. Notre Dame's transcription and page images carry 'Copyright (c) 2006, 2009, 2011 Dept. of Special Collections, University of Notre Dame' with no licence and no reuse terms; the transcript has editorial bracket notes and the collection introduction is by George Rugg. Human rights review needed.
items.evidence: Listed URL https://rarebooks.nd.edu/digital/civil_war/letters/sillers-holmes/5025-12.shtml: 301, 301, then 200 on the generic Rare Books home page (20,112 bytes), so a dead link in disguise. The new host's own digital index links 'Manuscripts of the American Civil War' to https://rarebooks.library.nd.edu/404-www3_sites.html, which says 'Site Currently Unavailable ... currently offline due to technical issues'. The legacy path on the new host returns HTTP 403 with an S3-style AccessDenied XML (111 bytes). I read that as a missing page, not a bot block, and did not retry. Wayback capture 20231211132213 (raw, 200, 34,933 bytes, sha256 c1d99860...): 'Sillers-Holmes Family Correspondence - August 7, 1863'; Author William W. Sillers; To Frances Sillers Holmes; Near Orange Court House, Virginia; 4 pages; MSN/CW 5025-12; 'Transcribed by: Paul Patterson and George Rugg, 2004-06'. Text: 'Ransom fell in with a party of pillaging soldiers at Gettysburg'; 'the Yankees got that bottle of Brandy, when they took our mess-chest at Waterloo Gap'; 'We spent three days very pleasantly at Carlisle ... Genl. Fitzhugh Lee burned all these buildings down'. Collection index (capture 20240730113049, 60,121 bytes): Sillers (1838-1863) was a Confederate officer, a major commanding the 30th North Carolina at Gettysburg (Ramseur's brigade, Rodes's division), made lieutenant colonel on 3 Sept 1863, mortally wounded 7 Nov 1863. The regiment is confirmed by the collection introduction, not by this letter. In the same collection, 5025-10 (16 July 1863, capture 20240730205932) is the battle letter: 'the most tremendous battle of the war', Pettigrew mortally wounded, Col. Parker wounded at Gettysburg.
items.extraction_notes: Static HTML (legacy shtml) with a labelled 'Transcription' block per page and 'Page 1..4' markers, so the html adapter works on the Wayback copy; the site is offline at the moment. Keep the 'Number: MSN/CW 5025-12' and 'Transcribed by' lines as provenance. Passages worth keeping are the Gettysburg pillaging remark and the Carlisle Barracks remark, about 2 to 3 paragraphs in all. If this collection is used at all, letter 5025-10 (16 July 1863) is the more useful one for the battle.
issues: Description says 'letter from the campaign': it is dated 7 August, after the retreat, and only recalls Carlisle and Gettysburg.
The list does not say which Sillers letter; only the link (5025-12) identifies it.
The legacy host now redirects to a generic page and the Civil War manuscripts site is shown as offline.
The transcription belongs to Notre Dame (copyright notice, no licence).

Wayback is the only readable copy.

items.evidence: Listed URL: 301 to https, then HTTP 404. Wayback capture 20231002015237 (raw, 200, 20,592 bytes): 'Boyhood Memories of The Civil War 1861-'65 - Invasion of Carlisle,' by James W. Sullivan; 46 pages; Date July 1932; Publisher Carlisle, PA: Hamilton Library Association; Location SC 974.8432 S949b; tags Invasion of Carlisle, Shelling of Carlisle, Burning of Barracks; the page's 'Year' field says 1863, which contradicts the 1932 date. PDF capture 20240622030747 (14,654,048 bytes, sha256 c090b254e0a63e998aec976497cb122662bc2a8ccdfbcf66db1fa2e830baff8e, 46 pp.): p.1 cover sheet, p.2 title page ('A Letter Written by James W. Sullivan in July, 1932, at Hereford, England, to His Friend, Jane Van Ness Smead ... 1933'), pp.3-46 the text with an OCR layer of about 106,000 characters. Text checked: 'In April, 1861 ... I had just reached the age of thirteen'; 'On July 1, 1863, I was awakened soon after dawn'; 'I can offer no more myself than the impression of an eye-witness during the Confederates' occupation of the town, with its climax the shelling ... that of a lad of fifteen'; he saw infantry passing the night of 30 June to 1 July; 'I heard the music of my first shell'; the Gettysburg battle is only mentioned in passing. Relevant passages: the arrival of the Confederates (Carlisle, 27 June), the Confederate soldiers' appearance, the night of 30 June to 1 July, the shelling. Contains slurs that need a content note.

Call to Arms', 2 pages, Date July 3, 1863, Location I-Original-1863-2, tags Battle of Gettysburg, Invasion of Pennsylvania, Shelling of Carlisle; the catalogue says it 'calls for all able men to enlist' and describes Confederate atrocities and the shelling of Carlisle. PDF capture 20240329143726 (369,941 bytes, sha256 aac107ea676d731bf3e693f5303aaaa6d68a68adaf6185cadfe4c235e0526363): p.1 cover sheet; p.2 one image of 1011x1376 pixels, which I viewed. Printed headings: 'CITIZENS OF THE CUMBERLAND VALLEY!' and 'Fellow-Citizens! Rise! Arm!'; text: 'The hour has come to arm! To every man now that can carry a musket, the line of duty is plain'; 'they have broken open our stores ... plundered peaceable farmers of their horses and cattle'; postscript: 'The printing of the few lines above was intercepted on Wednesday evening by the sudden and unexpected boom of the invaders cannon before Carlisle'; ends 'CARLISLE, July 3, 1863. [Circulate through the county.]'. A 6x enlargement of the date shows a worn day digit that looks like 3. Wednesday was 1 July 1863 (computed), so the broadside is after the shelling; the lines 'The foe is turned back. He is surrounded' could fit a date later than 3 July. 'Call to Arms' is the catalogue title, not printed on the sheet. Guessed new-site slug https://archives.dickinson.edu/document-descriptions/broadside-citizens-cumberland-valley-call-arms returns 404.
items.extraction_notes: Image only (one scan of the whole sheet). The PDF's OCR layer is garbled ('rnvn.ged', 'Ccstroy'), so use manual transcription: about 450 words, one column, readable at the native 1011x1376 resolution; a second person should check it against the image. Transcribe the date as 'July 3(?), 1863' and keep the printer-less, unsigned status. The corpus should treat it as propaganda: anonymous, with claims of atrocities and 'intercepted' printing.
issues: Day digit in the dateline is degraded; catalogue says 3 July, so 'issued during the battle' depends on that reading.
Anonymous propaganda broadside; its factual claims about plundering are unsupported.

Full text for only 6 of 50 items; the Chambersburg hospital and Col. Carter items have summaries only.

items.written: 1900 (SHSP vol. 28, article pp. 148-155), compiling records of March-June 1863
items.rights_basis: Internet Archive scan southernhistoric2819sout: metadata volume 'v.28(1900)', publisher 'Richmond, Virginia Historical Society'; the OCR title page reads 'RICHMOND, VA. Published by the Society. 1900'; 'possible-copyright-status: Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright'. Original imprint before 1931 with the year read from the title page, and the quoted records are US Government documents. This tier is for the Internet Archive copy, not the Perseus transcription (Tufts rights not checked).
items.evidence: The Perseus URL was not fetched: www.perseus.tufts.edu/robots.txt says Disallow: /. I found the same article in the Internet Archive scan. https://archive.org/metadata/southernhistoric2819sout: HTTP 200, 78,322 bytes: title 'Southern Historical Society papers', v.28(1900), 408 images, scanned 2015-04-24, sponsor University of Florida Smathers Libraries. https://archive.org/download/southernhistoric2819sout/southernhistoric2819sout_djvu.txt: HTTP 200, 1,077,008 bytes, sha256 8467b13f01c1608d4fc32b044963722889ee5636fba7655097402b18fc80ebef. Its table of contents lists 'XVII. The Correspondence of General R. E. Lee. Chancellorsville to Gettysburg - March to August, 1863. A pathetic array of evidence from the War Records, by Colonel Wm. H. Palmer 148'; the heading in the volume reads 'THE CORRESPONDENCE OF GEN. ROBT. E. LEE. Chancellorsville to Gettysburg - March to August, 1863'. Per the Archive's page_numbers.json, p.148 is leaf 162, p.155 is leaf 169, p.156 (next article) is leaf 170. Content read: a table of abstracts with OR page references (Series I, Vol. XXV pt. II, then Vol. XXVII pt. III), each line 'sender, date, page, addressee' plus a gist: e.g. 'R. E. Lee, April 20 ... to Davis. Insufficiency of cavalry', 'General Lee to General J. E. B. Stuart, June 22, 1863, page 913', 'General Lee to Davis, June 23, page 923', 'General Lee, Williamsport, June 25, 1863, to Davis'. Addressees also include Seddon, Cooper, A. P. Hill, Stuart; there are also letters from Seddon, Davis, Cooper, Jenkins to others. At the end (p.155): 'Mr. Davis' Letter to General Lee, June 28, 1863 ... was entrusted to a courier, who was captured by Captain Dahlgren, of General Meade's staff', and 'General Lee first learned that his suggestions would not be entertained by reading Mr. President Davis' letter in the New York Herald and New York Tribune', then 'GENERAL LEE RESIGNED IN AUGUST.' The compiler is named in the editor's note as 'Colonel William H. Palmer, formerly Chief of Staff of General A. P. Hill'; the editor's framing says the correspondence shows the army 'debilitated from being insufficiently fed'.
items.extraction_notes: Use the Internet Archive djvu text (adapter archive-fulltext). OCR is noisy, especially numerals and dates ('i86j' for 1863, 'page 8jS', 'Gettsyburg'), so check every date, page reference and quotation against the page image (leaves 162-169). The article is a table of one-line abstracts plus the editor's note (p.148-149) and the closing Davis note (p.155): the primary wording of the dispatches is in OR vol. 25 pt. 2 and vol. 27 pt. 3, which the project already ingests, so use this article for Palmer's framing and as a pointer, not as a source of Lee's words. Do not take Palmer's claims (Davis letter 'captured', Lee learned of it from a newspaper) as fact without OR support.
issues: Perseus link not checked; I could not confirm the mapping of its chapter 1.16 to this article, only the title and volume match the Internet Archive scan.

The article is longer than the entry says: March to August 1863 (the table itself runs to the end of June), many addressees, not only Davis; the Davis letter of 28 June is a note on the last page, not a calendar entry.
A 1900 compilation made to support an argument about Lee's shortages: retrospective advocacy.
Almost all of the content duplicates OR vol. 25 pt. 2 and vol. 27 pt. 3.
OCR layer is poor in the tables.
