summary: Independent second verification of entries 544, 552, 579, 598, 600, 601, 602, 604, re-derived from fetched sources. Verdicts: 544 APPROVE (A1), 552 APPROVE (A1, with a corrected two-article identity), 579 NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW (C, page anchor unverifiable), 598 APPROVE (A1), 600 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (C, with a corrected URL), 601 REJECT, 602 APPROVE (A1), 604 APPROVE (A1). I reached the same verdict and rights tier as the first pass on all eight, deciding before comparing. Where my evidence differs: (a) 579, the publisher's blurb on the Google page says the Gettysburg part of Brown's book comes from his memoir and the correspondence is for the later campaigns, which contradicts the first pass's 'correspondence, memoranda and diary'; (b) 598 and 604, complete single-volume Internet Archive scans of Wingate (Cornell and Harvard/Google) resolve the first pass's worry about the 'Pt. 1' item, and Garnett's p. 221 and Patterson's p. 214 anchors are right; (c) 602, Wingate p. 229 independently cites Leland pp. 254, 256 and 257, which confirms the Appleton pagination; (d) 552 holds two articles by two authors, and the 'Times-Dispatch reprint' remark does not attach to either; (e) 544 I compared the opening of the OR text in the repo's own OCR with SHSP: addressee and wording differ, so SHSP is not a reprint of the OR text. Not verified by anyone in this run: both Perseus targets (robots Disallow: /), the exact Google Books pg= pages (robots), the full text of the 600 article (219.6 MB issue PDF not downloaded), and any content of Campbell Brown p. 200. I did not launch a browser and made no repo edits.
systemic_findings: Part IX entries in this batch (579, 598, 600, 601, 602, 604) are a near-verbatim link list from House Divided's blog post 'Beyond Gettysburg: Primary Sources for the Gettysburg Campaign' (Cooper Wingert, posted 11 Jun 2018 and since extended; fetched, HTTP 200): the exact URLs, including the 'ftizhugh' typo and the Google Books dq/pg anchors, and the short descriptions ('wounded during the shelling', 'Civilian', 'Union') come from that page's hrefs and labels. Errors in those labels (601 is not an eyewitness) and links (600) therefore originate there.

Google Books pg= and dq= URLs cannot be fetched under Google's robots.txt (Disallow /books?*pg=, dq=); page content has to be verified through Internet Archive OCR of the same edition. For this batch that worked for 598 (PA221 = first page of Garnett's letter), 604 (PA214 = opening of Patterson's extract) and 602 (PA254 inside Leland's Carlisle account, which starts on p. 253), but not for 579, a limited-preview modern edition whose page content cannot be checked compliantly. The anonymous Google Books API returned HTTP 429 (quota 0), so it gave no viewability data.

Wingate's 1896 history (entries 598, 604) exists on IA as complete single-volume scans (Cornell cu31924030725166, 830 images; Harvard/Google historytwentyse00winggoog, 835 images) with identical pagination; the Allen County items historyoftwenty00wing (Pt. 1) and historyoftwentys00wing (Pt. 2) are a split binding. Prefer the complete scans for ingestion.

SHSP volumes have several IA scans each, and the University of Florida ones (southernhistoric7187sout, southernhistoric3719sout) carry the volume year ('v.7(1879)', 'v.37(1909)') and 'Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright' in their metadata, the best rights evidence available; the plan's SRC-08 already names vol. 37 (3719) but not vol. 7, which entry 544 needs. Perseus (robots 'User-agent: *' Disallow: /) must stay out of the pipeline; its chapter numbers could not be tested.

Link probers need a title check, not just a status code: gardnerlibrary.org answers HTTP 200 with a generic listing page for an unknown slug (soft 404), and its robots.txt asks for a 10 s crawl delay, which the project's 1.2 s default gap does not meet for that host.

Cross-source consistency checks that held: Garnett (p. 221-225) and Patterson (p. 214-217), Leland's Memoirs (pp. 253-262) and Gen. W. F. Smith's report all agree that Landis' battery fired about three shots at the July 1 bombardment of Carlisle; Wingate p. 229 cites Leland's Memoirs by Appleton page numbers that match the Cornell and LOC scans. Divergences worth flagging for the Historian: Leland's numbers (about ten thousand rebels) and barracks chronology differ from Garnett and Stuart (about 1,500 men; barracks burned during the bombardment).

Stuart's Aug 20, 1863 report appears in SHSP Vol. 7 (1879) and in OR vol. 27 pt. 2 (1889) with different wording of the salutation and some sentences, per my comparison of the SHSP OCR with the repo's own OR OCR; entry 544 should be tagged a variant printing of text the Historian already ingests.

items.written: Report dated 20 Aug 1863 (Stuart to Col. R. H. Chilton, covering 16 June to 24 July 1863); first printed in full in SHSP Vol. VII No. 9, Sept. 1879, pp. 401-434.
items.rights_basis: Imprint year read from the SHSP Vol. VII title page in the OCR ('January to December, 1879', Richmond, Geo. W. Gary printer). The University of Florida copy southernhistoric7187sout has IA metadata volume 'v.7(1879)' and 'Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright'. The text is a Confederate official report of 1863 in a US imprint before 1931.
items.evidence: The listed Perseus URL (doc=Perseus:text:2001.05.0120:chapter=9.72) was NOT fetched. I fetched www.perseus.tufts.edu/robots.txt (HTTP 200): the 'User-agent: *' block ends 'Disallow: /' with only /hopper/grants, research, about, collections and index.html allowed, and the /hopper/text allow line is commented out. I found the article independently through the IA advancedsearch API and read three scans: southernhistoricv7sout (Allen County PL, 608 images, OCR 1,759,239 bytes), the UF scan southernhistoric7187sout (610 images, 1,764,017 bytes) and the monthly issue sim_southern-historical-society-papers_1879-09_7_9 (Vol 7 Iss 9, 1879-09, 126,505 bytes). The title page reads 'Volume VII. January to December, 1879'; the contents list gives 'Report of General J. E. B. Stuart ... 401'. The p. 401 heading is 'The Gettysburg Campaign - Full Report of General J. E. B. Stuart' under 'Vol. VII. Richmond, Va., September, 1879. No. 9', identical to the entry title (my own read; all three OCRs agree). An editor's bracketed note says SHSP had printed only a fragment (Aug 1876) and now, through Major H. B. McClellan, gives 'the full text'. The report is headed 'Headquarters Cavalry Division, Army of Northern Virginia, August 20th, 1863. To Colonel R. H. Chilton' and runs pp. 401-434 (signature on p. 434, then list of inclosures A-E). Concrete checks: Aldie ('one of the most sanguinary cavalry battles of the war', p. 403) and Middleburg (pp. 402-408) are covered; so are the ride via Westminster and Hanover (pp. 412-414), Carlisle (pp. 414-415), Gettysburg July 2-3 (pp. 415-418) and the retreat to the Potomac and Shepherdstown (to p. 434). The 'Aldie, Middleburg and the ride' part is correct but incomplete. 'Reprinted' is not supported. The repo's own OCR of OR vol. 27 pt. 2 (historian-src/raw/or27/normalized-2.txt) opens the same Aug 20 report with a different salutation ('General:' and no addressee, 'on June 16' where SHSP has 'on the 16th day of June, 1863'), so the two printings differ in wording and I did not diff them further. The repo's OR index holds the report inside composite record or27-2:0565 (pp. 679-720), so the Historian already ingests this report from the OR. Circumstantial only: the article sits in issue No. 9 and the Perseus link says chapter=9.72, which is consistent but proves nothing.
items.extraction_notes: Ingest from the IA OCR (adapter archive-fulltext), never Perseus. Printed pp. 401-434 = leaves 409-442 of southernhistoricv7sout and leaves 413-446 of the UF scan. Keep the editor's bracketed headnote and the line '*[The ladies of the place ... ] Omit if published. - R. E. L.' (p. 412, Lee's marginal note retained in print) out of Stuart's own words. OCR errors seen: 'Westminister', line-end hyphens, 'K. H. Chilton' in one scan and 'R. H. Chilton' in another. Because the OR text of the same report is already ingested and differs slightly, tag this as a variant printing (provenance: Lee's annotated copy via McClellan) rather than as new text.
issues: Perseus target cannot be fetched by a program (robots Disallow: /); whether chapter=9.72 is this article is unverified. The perseus adapter must not be used.

Description says 'reprinted by the Society': SHSP presents the text as newly obtained full text, and the repo's OR27 OCR shows a differently worded version (salutation and small details). Not a reprint of the OR text, which came a decade later.
Description covers only Aldie, Middleburg and the ride; the report also covers Hanover, Carlisle, Gettysburg July 2-3 and the retreat to 24 July (34 printed pages).
SHSP Vol. 7 is not among the volumes in the plan's SRC-08 (4, 5, 6, 10, 23, 33, 37); add it (UF id southernhistoric7187sout).
Not a new source for the Historian: the same report is in OR27 pt. 2 (record or27-2:0565); value is as a cross-check of the text and for the Lost Cause-era editorial framing.

items.written: Talcott: 1909 (his article quotes a letter of 12 March 1909); McIntosh: about 1909; both printed in SHSP Vol. XXXVII, title page 1909.
items.rights_basis: SHSP Vol. XXXVII title page in the OCR: 'Richmond, Va. Published by the Society. 1909'. The UF copy southernhistoric3719sout carries IA metadata volume 'v.37(1909)' and 'Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright'. US imprint before 1931.
items.evidence: The Perseus link (doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A2001.05.0295%3Achapter%3D1.40) was NOT fetched (the robots.txt I read has 'User-agent: *' with 'Disallow: /'), so which article chapter=1.40 opens is unverified. I read SHSP Vol. XXXVII in the IA scans southernhistoricv37sout (Allen County PL, 392 images, OCR 932,457 bytes) and southernhistoric3719sout (UF, 398 images, 941,483 bytes; this is the volume the plan's SRC-08 already names). The entry's two titles are two separate articles by two authors. (1) 'Stuart's Cavalry in the Gettysburg Campaign, by Col. John S. Mosby. A Review by Col. T. M. R. Talcott': the printed contents list says p. 12, but the running head on p. 12 is 'Work of the Ordnance Bureau', and the article starts on printed p. 21 (leaf 33 in the Allen scan, leaf 39 in the UF scan) and ends p. 37. It opens with a letter from Col. Walter H. Taylor dated Norfolk, 12 March 1909 and reviews Mosby's book (1908). It argues that Lee's report is not unfair to Stuart and that Stuart failed to keep Lee informed. (2) 'Review of the Gettysburg Campaign by one who participated therein - David Gregg McIntosh', pp. 74-143 (signed on p. 143 'David Grigg McIntosh', and the errata correct the signature to Gregg). It surveys the whole campaign, disputes parts of Mosby's account, and on p. 91-92 says Mosby is 'largely responsible' for Stuart's choice of route. Description check: 'Early-1900s papers' is right (1909); 'defending Stuart' is inverted for Talcott; the 'reprinted from the Richmond Times-Dispatch' bracket occurs on other items in this volume (for example the Venable obituary on p. 61, readers' letters) and not on these two. The volume's actual defence of Stuart, R. H. McKim's 'A Reply to Colonel John S. Mosby' (p. 210), is not named in the entry.
items.extraction_notes: Ingest from the IA OCR (adapter archive-fulltext) as two separate documents by printed page: Talcott pp. 21-37 and McIntosh pp. 74-143, with authors added (the entry names none). Attribute the quoted Taylor letter (pp. 21-22) and Mosby's quoted passages to their own authors, not to Talcott. Do not trust the printed contents page (12) for Talcott. Treat both as 1909 argument by Lee-side participants or staff, with Lost Cause framing, not as evidence of what happened in 1863.
issues: The entry bundles two articles by different authors under one Perseus link; the link can open only one of them and the author names and page ranges are missing.
Description inverts Talcott's stance (critical of Stuart) and the Times-Dispatch reprint claim does not attach to either article.
Printed contents gives p. 12 for Talcott; the article is on pp. 21-37.
Perseus cannot be fetched by a program; use the IA scans.
Retrospective polemic written 46 years later: low value for events, useful for how the Stuart controversy was argued.

items.written: Brown's postwar memoir, composition date not established from anything I could read; modern annotated edition published 2001.
items.rights_basis: The Google Books page for id=8Utl4RLPEucC lists the edition as 'illustrated, reprint, annotated', LSU Press, 2001, ISBN 0807130192, 432 pages, with a 'Limited preview' and 'No eBook available'. A modern copyrighted edition with editor's apparatus and no open licence. Whether Brown's text had an earlier printing is not verified, so its old age does not make it free to reuse; counsel decides.
items.evidence: The listed URL carries dq= and pg=PA200 parameters that Google's robots.txt disallows (Disallow: /books?*dq= and /books?*pg=), so I did not fetch it. I fetched the bare page https://books.google.com/books?id=8Utl4RLPEucC (HTTP 200, 58,205 bytes). It names 'Campbell Brown's Civil War: With Ewell in the Army of Northern Virginia', editor Terry L. Jones, LSU Press, Oct 1, 2001. Its contents panel lists 'The Gettysburg Campaign 188', with the next listed chapter at p. 273, so p. 200 falls inside that chapter or just after its start, but I could not confirm that p. 200 is the Carlisle passage or that p. 200 is within the free preview. The publisher blurb on the page calls Brown 'cousin, stepson, and staff officer' of Ewell and says his memoir covers First Manassas through Gettysburg and Vicksburg, while his correspondence and memoranda cover the Overland Campaign to Sayler's Creek and his Fort Warren letters; so the Gettysburg portion is memoir, contrary to the first pass's 'correspondence, memoranda and diary'. The anonymous Google Books API returned HTTP 429 (quota 0), so no accessInfo was available. Provenance of the entry: House Divided's blog post 'Beyond Gettysburg: Primary Sources for the Gettysburg Campaign' (Cooper Wingert, 11 Jun 2018; fetched HTTP 200) lists 'Campbell Brown account (Confederate Staff Officer)' under 'Confederate Occupation of Carlisle - June 27-28, 1863' with exactly this URL (pg=PA200), so the page anchor is House Divided's own citation, not mine.
items.extraction_notes: No text can be extracted: copyrighted edition and Google's robots bar fetching the page. Link-out only. If a human opens the link and it lands on Brown's June 27-28 Carlisle narrative inside the preview, cite as Campbell Brown's Civil War (LSU Press, 2001), ed. Terry L. Jones, p. 200, and describe it as the editor's edition of a postwar memoir.
issues: Page-level content (that p. 200 is the Carlisle occupation, and that it is viewable in the preview) is not verified; Google's robots.txt prevents a compliant check.
Modern copyrighted edition (LSU Press 2001, annotated): link-out only, never quote.

Entry describes the content as 'memoir pages': the publisher blurb supports memoir for the Gettysburg part, but the book as a whole is a mixed edition (memoir, correspondence, memoranda, prison letters).
Possible limited-preview gap: a human should confirm page 200 appears in the preview before approving the link-out.

items.written: Letter dated Norfolk, Va., 31 May 1892 (29 years after the event), to Gen. George W. Wingate; printed in Wingate's History of the Twenty-second Regiment, 1896, pp. 221-225.
items.rights_basis: Title page of the Cornell scan (OCR): 'History of the Twenty-second Regiment of the National Guard of the State of New York from its Organization to 1895, by General George W. Wingate, New York: Edwin W. Dayton ... Copyright, 1896'. Cornell note 'no known copyright restrictions in the United States'; IA metadata date 1896; the Harvard/Google scan has 'possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT, US'. The Google page offers PDF/EPUB download (full view). The letter was first printed in this book.
items.evidence: The exact URL (dq=, pg=PA221) was not fetched (robots). The bare page https://books.google.com/books?id=CJQQAAAAYAAJ (HTTP 200, 97,662 bytes) names Wingate, E. W. Dayton, 1896, 762 pages, original from Harvard, with Download PDF/EPUB (full view); its metadata calls it 'Volume 22, Part 4', a catalogue artefact. I found two complete single-volume scans on IA and read both: Cornell cu31924030725166 (830 images, OCR 1,372,744 bytes) and the Harvard/Google scan historytwentyse00winggoog (835 images, OCR 1,387,819 bytes); Harvard is also the source of the Google Books copy. The Allen County items historyoftwenty00wing (Pt. 1) and historyoftwentys00wing (Pt. 2) are a split binding and were not needed. In both scans the running head 221 is followed by 'Norfolk, Va., May 31, 1892. Gen. George W. Wingate, New York. Dear General - In response to your request ... of the twenty-seventh instant, I proceed to give you an account of the advance upon Carlisle'. The page map puts printed p. 221 at leaf 260 (Cornell) and leaf 261 (Harvard), so the PA221 anchor is the first page of the letter. Wingate's lead-in on p. 220 names 'Col. T. S. Garnet, aid to Gen. Stuart'; the signature on p. 225 reads 'Theodore S. Garnet, Late Aide-de-Camp to Gen. J. E. B. Stuart' (contents and index spell it Garnett). Two concrete claims: only Fitz Lee's brigade, 'about 1,500 men' and four guns, invested Carlisle; and the shelling began after a flag of truce was refused, with his first two shells from the hill landing among his own men in the dark (p. 223). He also says Stuart's absence from the main army at Gettysburg was not imputable to any fault of Stuart (p. 225). The description is accurate. Provenance: House Divided's post (fetched) lists 'Theodore S. Garnett account (Confederate)' with this exact PA221 URL.
items.extraction_notes: Take pp. 221-225 from the Cornell OCR (adapter archive-fulltext). Two rows of asterisks mark passages Wingate left out (after the opening sentence on p. 221 and at the end of p. 225), so it is an extract, not the whole letter. The footnotes marked *, dagger and double dagger on pp. 222-225 are Wingate's, not Garnett's, and the quotation of Stuart's OR report (pp. 223-224) and of Gen. W. F. Smith's report is Stuart's and Smith's. OCR variants: 'Garnet', 'Aidede-Camp'. Add the Harvard scan as a second witness for any contested word.
issues: Exact Google Books URL cannot be fetched (robots); the PA221 anchor was confirmed instead from the printed page numbers of two IA scans of the same edition.
Wingate's printing is elided (asterisks) and carries his own footnotes; the letter is a recollection from 1892, with the usual retrospective bias, and ends with a defence of Stuart.
The first pass worried the IA item was labelled 'Pt. 1': the Cornell and Harvard/Google scans are complete single volumes and match the Google page (p. 221), so use those.
Name spelled 'Garnet' in the signature and 'Garnett' in the index and the entry.

items.written: 2013 (Cumberland County History, Vol. 30); author Rachael Zuch.
items.rights_basis: The Gardner Library pages carry 'Copyright 2014-2026 Cumberland County Historical Society All rights reserved'; a modern article with no open licence shown. Peer-review status not stated.
items.evidence: Honouring the robots.txt 'Crawl-delay: 10' (I waited at least 10.5 s between requests). The listed URL http://gardnerlibrary.org/journal/ftizhugh-lee-reconciling-north-and-south-carlisle-pa answers 301 to https, then HTTP 200 with the generic title 'CCHS Publications Browsing' (an index of journal issues by year), so it is a soft 404 that does not show the article. House Divided's post (fetched) carries the same typo 'ftizhugh' in its own link, so the error originates there. The corrected slug https://gardnerlibrary.org/journal/fitzhugh-lee-reconciling-north-and-south-carlisle-pa returns HTTP 200 (22,685 bytes) with the title 'Fitzhugh Lee: Reconciling North and South in Carlisle, PA', author Zuch, Rachael, 'Journal Issue: 2013, Volume 30'. The page shows an abstract only; its 'Read the entire article' link points to vol30n1.pdf#page=79, a 219,583,236-byte issue PDF (HEAD request only, last-modified 29 Mar 2018), which I did not download. The abstract says the 1863 shelling was ordered by Stuart and carried out by Fitzhugh Lee, that Lee had been a cavalry instructor at Carlisle Barracks in 1856-1858, and that the article is about Lee's welcome on a return visit 33 years after the shelling and the national mood of reconciliation. So the description 'Lee's role at Carlisle and his later reconciliation visits' fits only roughly: the article is mainly about postwar reconciliation, the shelling is background, and it describes a return visit rather than visits. I did not read the article body.
items.extraction_notes: Link-out only. Cite as Rachael Zuch, 'Fitzhugh Lee: Reconciling North and South in Carlisle, PA', Cumberland County History 30 (2013), using the corrected URL. Do not quote (copyrighted) and do not download the 219 MB issue PDF; use the abstract page for the citation card.
issues: Listed URL has a typo ('ftizhugh', copied from House Divided's post) and serves a generic listing page with HTTP 200 (soft 404): a link checker must compare the page title.

The article body was not read (abstract only), so its factual claims are unchecked; the abstract page itself calls Fitzhugh Lee 'Major General' for July 1863, whereas Stuart's report as printed in SHSP Vol. VII calls him 'Brigadier-General Fitz. Lee' in June 1863 (a rank anachronism on the host page).
Primarily a postwar-reconciliation article: little Gettysburg-campaign evidence.
gardnerlibrary.org robots.txt asks for a 10 s crawl delay; any future probe should wait at least that long.

items.written: Foreword dated 14 June 1937; the author (born 6 Jan 1864 in Carlisle) retells a story her mother told, about 74 years after the event.
items.rights_basis: No licence or rights statement on the PDF. It is a 1937 typescript from the Wyoming State Archives (header text on page 1), apparently unpublished; the author's death date and the rights holder are unknown, so no tier can be justified by evidence.
items.evidence: housedivided.dickinson.edu/robots.txt returned 404 (no restrictions). The listed http URL answers 301 to https, then HTTP 200 application/pdf, 1,080,976 bytes (sha256 1f274eeebdeffdafc44100176d485aff3c5e3eef7e4beed7cfd8f847a78ca60a), 3 pages, each a single scanned image with no text layer, so I rendered and read all three. Page 1 (header 'Wyoming State Archives'): 'FOREWORD ... The incidents related in this article, THE ARGESHEIMER FAMILY, are given from my own knowledge of the people and events mentioned therein', signed (Mrs) Anna M. M. Fosdick, dated June 14th 1937. Page 2: 'THE ARGESHEIMER FAMILY by MRS. ANNA (ARGESHEIMER) FOSDICK'; her father John Henry Argesheimer, a German-born army musician (b. 13 Feb 1836); her mother Harriet Lavenia Wallace (b. 26 Dec 1837 at Gettysburg), married at Carlisle about 1860. The only Carlisle shelling passage is about seven sentences: 'I remember hearing her tell of the time the Rebels made an attack on Carlisle', with exchanged wounded Union prisoners being fed in the market place by Carlisle's women, her mother among them, until shells burst over the market. Page 3 lists the children and says Anna Mary Magdalene was born at Carlisle on 6 January 1864 and then moves to the family's 1875 move to Fort D. A. Russell, Wyoming, and Cheyenne, with no more on 1863. So Anna was born six months after the event and is repeating her mother's story: second-hand, not 'a Carlisle woman's recollection of the shelling'. House Divided's post (fetched) lists the item as 'Anna Fosdick recollection (Civilian)' with this URL.
items.extraction_notes: Image-only PDF (needs manual transcription); the relevant lines are on PDF page 2. Not suitable for the quote corpus: hearsay from a woman born after the event, a few lines inside an unrelated family history, rights unknown. If a human wants it as a pointer, describe it as 'Anna Fosdick (b. 1864), 1937 family-history typescript repeating her mother's account of the Carlisle shelling', never as an eyewitness account.
issues: Description is wrong: the author was born in 1864 and relays her mother's story; she is not an eyewitness.
Typescript from the Wyoming State Archives, not a Carlisle source; rights and provenance unknown (1937 unpublished item; no licence).
Content is a few sentences inside a family history; image-only PDF with no text layer.
The mother's detail (exchanged wounded prisoners fed in the market place) is unconfirmed hearsay and not checked against any other source.

items.written: Printed 1893 (D. Appleton); the Emergency of June-July 1863 recalled about 30 years later, with later notes; includes R. W. Gilder's letter to Leland on pp. 266-268.
items.rights_basis: Title page of the Cornell scan (OCR): 'Memoirs by Charles Godfrey Leland (Hans Breitmann), New York: D. Appleton and Company, 1893', 'Copyright, 1893'. Cornell note 'no known copyright restrictions in the United States'; the Library of Congress scan memoirs00lela has 'The Library of Congress is unaware of any copyright restrictions for this item'. US imprint before 1931.
items.evidence: The listed URL (dq=, pg=PA254) was not fetched (robots). The bare page https://books.google.com/books?id=O7Ud9eFYGWcC (HTTP 200, 67,529 bytes) shows 'Memoirs, Charles Godfrey Leland, D. Appleton, 1893, 439 pages', full view with PDF/EPUB download. I read two IA scans of the same Appleton edition: Cornell cu31924022024081 (474 images, OCR 942,091 bytes; ends at p. 439 with the Appleton advertisements) and the Library of Congress memoirs00lela (472 images, OCR 1,094,894 bytes; page map puts printed p. 254 at leaf 272). The chapter '1862-1866' has the running head 'Life during the Civil War'. On p. 251-252 Leland says he went as a 'full private' in an artillery company whose captain was 'a dealer in cutlery named Landis'; the Carlisle shelling starts at the foot of p. 253 ('Hearing that the rebels were threatening Carlisle, we were sent thither on a forced march of sixteen miles') and p. 254 holds the lamp-post and grape-shot passage and Landis's remark about shells, so PA254 lands in the middle of the account. On p. 262 he says 'we were not put under fire at Gettysburg, but kept in Smith's reserve'. Independent cross-check: Wingate's history (pp. 229-231, Cornell scan) quotes Leland's Memoirs with page cites 'p. 254', 'p. 256' (Stuart Patterson's right-hand fingers cut away by a shell) and 'p. 257' (his brother's wound), all of which match the passages in the Appleton scans, confirming that pagination. Accuracy of the entry's wording ('Writer and militia volunteer's account of the emergency campaign'): yes. Caution: Leland's chronology is loose (he says the rebels 'had been before us, and partially burned the barracks' whereas Garnett and Stuart place the barracks fire during the July 1 bombardment) and he writes 'about ten thousand rebel regulars' where Garnett says about 1,500. Provenance: House Divided's post lists 'Charles Godfrey Leland memoir (Union)' with this exact URL.
items.extraction_notes: Take the Emergency narrative pp. 251-262 and Gilder's letter pp. 266-268 from the OCR (adapter archive-fulltext); use only the Appleton (New York, 1893, 439 pp.) text, since the Heinemann London edition is in two volumes with different pagination. Anecdotal and humorous prose with hearsay and later footnotes (for example the 'Come and take it' note on p. 267): label as retrospective, and tag Gilder's letter as Gilder's, not Leland's. Not an account of the battle: his battery stayed in W. F. Smith's reserve.
issues: Page anchor cannot be fetched on Google Books for bots; confirmed through the printed pagination of two IA scans and Wingate's own page cites.
Retrospective (c. 1890s) anecdotal prose with humour and hearsay; chronology and numbers are unreliable against Garnett and the OR.
Appleton edition only: the Heinemann London edition has different pagination, so the Google/IA copy must be the Appleton one.
The Carlisle account begins on p. 253 and runs to about p. 262, so a citation should give the range, not p. 254 alone.

items.written: Undated letter, written before 1896 (printed in Wingate's 1896 history, pp. 214-217); it mentions Wingate's earlier 'admirable description' of the march, which I take to be his 1864 pamphlet, but that is an inference.
items.rights_basis: Same book as entry 598: Wingate, History of the Twenty-second Regiment, New York: Edwin W. Dayton, 'Copyright, 1896' (title page of the Cornell scan); IA metadata 1896; Cornell 'no known copyright restrictions'; Harvard/Google scan 'NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT, US'. The letter is not known to have been printed before this book.
items.evidence: The exact URL (dq=, pg=PA214) was not fetched (robots); the bare page (same book as 598, HTTP 200) names Wingate, E. W. Dayton, 1896, 762 pages, full view. In both complete IA scans (Cornell cu31924030725166 and Harvard/Google historytwentyse00winggoog) the page map puts printed p. 214 at leaf 253 (Cornell) and leaf 254 (Harvard). Printed p. 214 begins mid-sentence 'Landis' Battery to proceed, with all possible speed, to Carlisle' and continues 'The following extract from a letter from C. Stuart Patterson, a member of the battery who was severely wounded during the engagement, gives a graphic account of their experiences', so the PA214 anchor is the first page of the extract. The extract runs to p. 217 and ends with 'Just as I had given the order to fire the third shot ... I received the wound which consigned me to the hospital for the balance of that fight and sent me home two days afterwards.' Concrete claims: the section galloped to Carlisle, reaching the market square near dusk, where citizens served food; the first shell passed overhead while he sat on a curbstone; his gun went into battery on the railway track against a battery about 300 yards off; the battery 'fired ... but three shots', which matches Gen. W. F. Smith's report as quoted by Wingate on p. 225 (Landis' battery replied with three); and 'Hans Breitman (Charles S. Leland)' rode astride a gun on the way. 'Wounded during the shelling' is verified three ways: Wingate's lead-in (p. 214), Patterson's own words (p. 217), and Leland's Memoirs as quoted by Wingate on p. 229 and in the Appleton scans (p. 256: four fingers of his right hand cut away by a shell). The entry's wording matches House Divided's label 'C. Stuart Patterson account (Union) - wounded during the shelling' in its post (fetched), which carries this exact URL.
items.extraction_notes: Take pp. 214-217 from the Cornell OCR (adapter archive-fulltext); the extract begins after Wingate's lead-in sentence on p. 214 and ends before Wingate's narrative resumes on p. 217. Opening words are in quotation marks and the letter is printed as an 'extract', so omissions are possible but not marked. The index lists Patterson at pp. 214 and 229, but p. 229 is Leland and Gilder quoting about him, not his own words. No addressee or date is printed.
issues: Undated letter; composition date only bounded (before 1896; probably after Wingate's 1864 account of the march, by inference).
Anchor PA214 cannot be fetched on Google Books; confirmed from the printed page numbers of two IA scans, not by seeing the Google page.
Humorous recollection: details such as distances (300 yards) and numbers are unchecked against the OR; its three-shot figure agrees with Smith's report as quoted by Wingate.
Wingate's lead-in and later footnotes are Wingate's words, not Patterson's.

summary:
Second independent verification of entries 618, 622, 623, 627, 628, 630, 631 and 632, re-derived from my own fetches (log of every request: the file log.txt in the scratchpad folder qcb-618-632). No browser; one request at a time with at least 1.3 s between requests (10 s on scholarworks.uvm.edu, which sets Crawl-delay 10); the honest Gettysburg-sources-QC user agent; robots.txt read first on every host. The Google Books listed URLs (dq= and pg= parameters) and Chronicling America were not fetched; the bare Google Books ?id= pages are not disallowed and were fetched. No repository file was written.

Result: 3 APPROVE (622, 627, 628: pre-1931 imprints with the year read from the title page or Archive metadata; text taken from Internet Archive scans) and 5 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (618, 623, 630, 631, 632). My verdict, rights tier and kind agree with the first pass on all 8. I found differences only in the evidence and detail:
- 622: the pg=PA97 anchor is printed p. 97, a page about removing valuables. Chambersburg's seizure of Black residents is on pp. 107-109, with the Schaff diary quote on p. 96.
- 628: the first pass's open question about an A. K. McClure introduction is resolved. The scan's unsigned introduction ends with the initials a. k. m., and the Google Books table of contents says 'Introduction by A K McClure'.
- 623: the PDF is S. K. Donavin's article in Cumberland County History 15:1 (Summer 1998), pp. 34-50. The host's page, found by a web search and then fetched, states this. I propose a replacement landing page.
- 630: the PDF's text is identical to pp. 157-158 of the entry 631 book (whitespace-normalised comparison, both pages).
- 631: the old viewcontent.cgi link returns HTTP 200 with only a DSpace shell. The legacy URL https://scholarworks.uvm.edu/crvocc/21 (no trailing slash) and /handle/20.500.14849/1322 both 301 to /items/9df80ca3-4c1b-4e03-9b9e-b2e3e1f31c13. The repository labels the item CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, while the book itself says 'All rights reserved' (2002). The book's pp. 155-156 hold the July 1 and July 9, 1863 letters, which describe the Sixth Corps' march to Gettysburg and its position on July 2-3. The first pass did not mention these, and the excerpt in 630 begins only at the tail of the July 9 letter.
- 618: the web text is the 1978 printed edition (Friends of the University of Iowa Libraries; notes by Edwin C. Bearss; editorial punctuation).

Not verified: any Google Books page anchor; the 1978, 1998 and 2002 copyright notices and renewals; whether an original Donavin newspaper page is available free (Chronicling America returned a Cloudflare challenge and was not pursued); the Valley of the Shadow site's current copy of the Creigh item; the original Creigh diary.
systemic_findings: Dickinson House Divided: the three PDFs I fetched on housedivided.dickinson.edu (/library/Donavin1998.pdf and /sites/blogdivided/files/2018/06/...) are live (HTTP 301 http to https, then 200), and the host's robots.txt is 404 (no rules). The dead-link pattern (404) found earlier is specific to the Dickinson Archives paths and should not be applied to every housedivided.dickinson.edu URL.

Google Books links in the list carry dq= and pg= parameters that robots.txt disallows, so page anchors cannot be checked by a bot. For Hoke (622, 628) the Internet Archive scans verified the passages; the Archive's search-inside API (fulltext/inside.php) plus page_numbers.json gives a leaf and a printed page for a quoted phrase, which is a polite way to check such anchors.

The 622 anchor pg=PA97 is the page on removal of valuables, not the passage about the seizure of Black residents (pp. 107-109, plus the Schaff quote on p. 96): anchors in this list should not be trusted for what the description says.

The Internet Archive holds several scans of the same Hoke editions and a 1959 reprint (bwb_Y0-BDN-722) of the 1887 book; the allow-list must pin an identifier (greatinvasionof100hoke for 1887, reminiscencesofw00hoke for 1884).

UVM ScholarWorks migrated from bepress to DSpace: old viewcontent.cgi links return HTTP 200 with a 827 B shell page (a dead link that a status check reports as live). Legacy item paths without a trailing slash (https://scholarworks.uvm.edu/crvocc/21) and /handle/ paths redirect to /items/<uuid>; the host sets Crawl-delay 10. The repository assigned CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 to the item while the book's own notice says All rights reserved.

Several list entries are not what their titles say: 623 is a 1998 journal reprint, 630 is a two-page excerpt of the book in 631, 632 is a 1940 paper quoting a diary, 618 is the 1978 printed edition republished on a blog. Rights tiers and kinds should be set from the edition actually hosted, not from the 1863-65 date of the underlying writing.

Chronicling America now redirects to loc.gov and answers a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403); I did not try to get past it. The Wayback CDX endpoint answered 503 (temporarily offline) once during this run, while capture pages loaded normally.

Of the 8 entries, only the three pre-1931 imprints (622, 627, 628) can feed the quote corpus, all through Internet Archive scans; the five others are link-out or facts only because the host text is a modern edition, a copyrighted reprint, or of unknown rights.

Environment note: other workflow agents write into the shared scratchpad folder (a helper script of mine was overwritten once by another agent's file of the same name), so all my files for this batch are in the private subfolder qcb-618-632 of the scratchpad.

items.written: 1863-06-27 (letter, Gallatin, Tenn.); web text from the 1978 printed edition
items.rights_basis: Letter by Joseph F. Culver (1834-1899 per the site's introduction): the 1863 text is old and public domain. The web text is the 1978 book edition (Friends of the University of Iowa Libraries; editor Leslie W. Dunlap; notes by Edwin C. Bearss) with editorial paragraphing, punctuation, spelling corrections and bracketed insertions. No copyright or licence statement on the three site pages I fetched; the book's own notice and renewal are not verified.
items.evidence: Fetched https://blog.lib.uiowa.edu/culver/1863/6-27b/ (HTTP 200, 42,905 B, canonical URL equal to the listed one; host robots.txt disallows only /wp-admin/). Heading: Head Quarters, Co. A, 129th Ills., Gallatin, Tenn., June 27th 1863, 'Dear Mary', signed J. F. Culver. Claim 1 (concern for his father in Carlisle): the letter says he learned from the papers that Carlisle is in possession of the Rebels and he fears the shock to Father; an editor's note says Joseph Culver, J.F.C.'s father, was 72 and lived in Carlisle's East Ward. Claim 2 (Union soldier): 129th Illinois, Gallatin, Tennessee. The other June 27 post (/culver/1863/06-27/, fetched) never mentions Carlisle (0 hits), so the listed 6-27b is the right post. The site's Introduction page is the 1978 book introduction signed Leslie W. Dunlap, July 19, 1978; the About page names the book Your Affectionate Husband, J.F. Culver: Letters Written During the Civil War; the editor says paragraph breaks and punctuation were added and misspellings corrected. Footnote cites Wilbur S. Nye, Here Come the Rebels (1965).
items.extraction_notes: Plain HTML (adapter html). The letter body is clean, but footnotes are inline in double parentheses and must be stripped (they are Bearss's 1978 notes, not Culver). Editorial additions appear in square brackets. The entry's only Gettysburg-campaign content is one sentence of news reception, written 600 miles away; low value for the quote corpus.
issues: Title 'Joseph Culver letter' omits the F.; the writer is Joseph F. Culver, not his 72-year-old father Joseph Culver.
The writer was in Tennessee: no first-hand knowledge of Carlisle or the invasion, only news reception.
Listed under 'Campaign eyewitness accounts', which it is not.
Web text is a 1978 edited transcription with editorial apparatus; no licence statement found.
The same site has a second June 27 post (06-27) that does not mention Carlisle.

items.written: 1887 (published); Chambersburg events of June 1863 recalled from Hoke's own record, other chapters compiled
items.rights_basis: Title page of the Internet Archive scan reads Dayton, Ohio: W. J. Shuey, Publisher, 1887, with Copyright 1887 by W. J. Shuey. Archive metadata: date 1887, publisher Dayton, O., W. J. Shuey, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT, contributor New York Public Library. Original imprint before 1931. Hoke died 1893 (Archive creator field 1825-1893).
items.evidence: Google Books: robots.txt disallows dq= and pg= parameters, so I fetched only https://books.google.com/books?id=JbMTAAAAYAAJ (HTTP 200): Jacob Hoke, W. J. Shuey, 1887, 613 pages, Original from the New York Public Library, Digitized Jan 7, 2008, Full view, Download PDF/EPUB offered. Internet Archive item greatinvasionof100hoke (metadata API 200; NYPL scan, 644 images, 'xxxi, [33]-613 p.'); djvu text 1,306,574 B downloaded and read. Title page: THE GREAT INVASION OF 1863; OR, GENERAL LEE IN PENNSYLVANIA ... With an Appendix ... JACOB HOKE. Claim 1 (Chambersburg merchant who witnessed the invasion): printed p. 97 says the firm 'of which the writer was a member' shipped and hid its dry goods in June 1863. Claim 2 (seizure of Black residents): pp. 107-108 (running head Capture of Negroes, p. 109) describe cavalry searching fields and houses for negroes on the day Jenkins entered; Hoke secured the release of two captured persons through a friend with influence with Jenkins; p. 96 quotes Dr. Schaff's diary that negroes were captured and carried into slavery, including free-born ones. The listed anchor pg=PA97 corresponds to printed p. 97 (removal of valuables), not the seizure passages (pp. 96 and 107-109). The Archive also holds a 1959 reprint (bwb_Y0-BDN-722) and other 1887 scans (greatinvasionof102hoke, cu31924030913846, greatinvasionofo00hokeiala).
items.extraction_notes: Use adapter archive-fulltext on greatinvasionof100hoke_djvu.txt (no page separators; printed page heads such as '96  THE GREAT INVASION.' are in the OCR and usable for page citation; 'Page 97' = REMOVAL OF VALUABLES head). Pin to this identifier or another 1887 scan, never the 1959 reprint. OCR has errors (e.g. 'W;is'), so verify quotes against page images. The book is a compilation: only the Chambersburg and Franklin County chapters are Hoke's own eyewitness (retrospective), the battle chapters are secondary.
issues: Description understates scope: whole campaign, three days of battle, retreat, plus an appendix; not only the Chambersburg invasion.
Entry anchor pg=PA97 does not point at the Black-residents passages (pp. 96 and 107-109).
Retrospective (1887) and openly Unionist in tone; much of the battle narrative is second-hand.
Google Books page anchors cannot be checked by a bot (robots), so link identity rests on the bare id page plus the matching Archive scan (NYPL, same 613-page edition).
Other editions on the Archive (1959 reprint) must be kept off any allow-list.

items.written: 1863-07-09 (Carlisle American Volunteer); reprinted 1998 (Cumberland County History, vol. 15, no. 1, Summer 1998)
items.rights_basis: The linked file is an image scan of pp. 34-50 of a 1998 journal issue, with an editor's introduction, spelling and punctuation corrections, a name added from the Herald, photographs, and a section of other June 1863 items. The publisher's site states 'Copyright 2014-2026 Cumberland County Historical Society All rights reserved'. The 1863 newspaper text is public domain, but this host copy is not a clean verbatim transcript.
items.evidence: housedivided.dickinson.edu robots.txt is 404 (no rules). Fetched http://housedivided.dickinson.edu/library/Donavin1998.pdf in full: 301 to https, then 200 application/pdf, 14,277,065 B, sha256 ae5f17cab07e9e4fc1c29abb207cc234336f84cda9622f7d614b5c2cc80ec828, Last-Modified 15 Jul 2010, 17 pages, no text layer (Acrobat image conversion). I rendered and read pages 1, 2, 3, 5, 12, 14, 15, 16 and 17. Page 1 (printed p. 34) is headed The Invasion: Rebel Occupancy of Carlisle, 1863, S.K. Donavin; the editor's note says the account was printed in the American Volunteer on July 9, 1863, the Herald on July 10 and the American on July 15, and is reprinted from the Volunteer with only a few spelling and punctuation changes and Ewell's name corrected. Claim 1 (occupation): printed p. 38 has Jenkins's advance entering Carlisle about eleven o'clock Saturday morning (June 27) after Col. Penrose and Robert Allison met him. Claim 2 (newspaper reprint): printed pp. 45-48 describe the July 1 arrival of Gen. W. F. Smith, the arrival of Fitzhugh Lee's cavalry, shelling of the town, flag of truce and burning of the barracks. Printed pp. 49-50 add separate June 18, 1863 American Volunteer items (Milroy's wagon train, the Chambersburg raid) and a Carlisle Herald July 10 sufferers list. A web search (not a host fetch) led to https://gardnerlibrary.org/journal/invasion-rebel-occupancy-carlisle-1863, which I then fetched (robots allows it): Journal Issue 1998 Summer, Volume 15, Issue 1, Author Donavin, S. K., link to the full-issue PDF vol15n1.pdf page 36; same introductory text. Chronicling America (via loc.gov) answered a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403); not circumvented, so I could not check for a public-domain original page.

items.written: 1884 (serialised in Public Opinion from 1884-01-12, then book); events of 1861-65, Gettysburg campaign recalled 21 years later
items.rights_basis: Title page of the Library of Congress scan on the Internet Archive: Historical Reminiscences of the War; or Incidents which transpired in and about Chambersburg, during the War of the Rebellion. By J. Hoke. Chambersburg, Pa.: M. A. Foltz, Printer and Publisher. 1884 (Copyrighted by M. A. Foltz, 1884). Archive metadata: date 1884, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT, contributor Library of Congress. Original imprint before 1931.
items.evidence: Google Books: only the bare page https://books.google.com/books?id=8F_WAAAAMAAJ was fetched (HTTP 200): Jacob Hoke, M.A. Foltz printer and publisher, 1884, 211 pages, Original from Pennsylvania State University, Digitized Jun 2, 2009; table of contents lists 'INTRODUCTION by A K McClure Esq'. The pg=PA38 anchor was not fetched (robots). Internet Archive reminiscencesofw00hoke (LoC scan, 228 images; djvu text 1,309,793 B read). The unsigned introduction ends with the initials a. k. m. and says Mr. Hoke witnessed every invasion of the town; this resolves the McClure question. Hoke's Note by the Author says his own record, written at the time, survived the 1864 burning. Passage checked: the Archive's search-inside API places 'Esque Hall' on leaf 44, which the Archive's page_numbers.json labels printed page 38, matching the entry's PA38. Text: soldiers scoured the fields for negroes; Esque Hall, a well known colored man, was carried off behind a rebel; Hoke fetched Dr. Schneck, who vouched to Jenkins that Hall was a long-time resident, not a fugitive, and Hall was released; Schneck told Hoke that a Jenkins staff officer who had heard Schneck preach in Virginia helped. Chapter VIII, Jenkins' Raid, starts p. 33; Chapter X is the wounded train from Gettysburg (p. 84), Chapter XVIII three visits to Gettysburg (p. 171).
items.extraction_notes: Adapter archive-fulltext on reminiscencesofw00hoke_djvu.txt (use the Library of Congress scan; the Gettysburg College copy reminiscences00hoke lacks a date field). No form feeds in the text; page numbers are mostly missing in the OCR, so cite page numbers through the Archive's page_numbers.json plus the search-inside leaf (leaf = printed page + 6 in this range). The Schneck passage is Hoke's first-person account (he fetched Schneck); the exchange between Schneck and Jenkins is secondhand.
issues: The Google Books pg=PA38 anchor could not be checked by a bot; the Archive scan confirms the passage is on printed p. 38.
The Archive catalog title drops the word Historical; the title page has it.
Retrospective (1884, 21 years after) and Union civilian.
Book also covers Gettysburg aftermath (chapters X, XII, XVIII); the cited passage is Jenkins's raid of June 1863.

summary:
Second verification of batch 352, 388, 424, 460, 496, 532, 728, 868, 1008, 1113. I decided all ten from my own fetches before comparing with the first pass. Method: the Internet Archive items warofrebellion272unit (OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 2) and warofrebellion273unit (pt. 3). I fetched their metadata, scandata, MARC record and per-page OCR (_djvu.xml) and viewed page images for printed pp. 81, 213 and 555. I also read the Civil War Cycling index the list took its titles and page ranges from. Wayback Machine captures of the four eHistory pages were fetched; eHistory itself was not. HathiTrust was not fetched.

Result: all six OR reports are APPROVE (A1). They are real, correctly numbered and attributed, and sit on the stated pages. All four Part XIII pages are APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (A1 for the underlying text). Pointers are not writings, and the eHistory link could only be checked through 2021 archive captures. My verdicts and tiers match the first pass on all 10. The differences are small. I classed 868 as dispatch-or-order, where the first pass said compiled-volume. I used not-fetched for the eHistory links. And I found two things the first pass did not mention:
- The IA scan clips the left margin on several pt. 2 pages, so the OCR drops characters.
- The OCR has numeral errors, with two confirmed on page images.

Descriptions: 4 of the 6 reports are partly inaccurate against the one-line template. 352 is Winchester, 388 is a supplementary report written by an officer absent from the fighting, 496 has no marches, and 532 is Aldie. 868 is partly inaccurate because the page is mostly a statistical table.

Not verified: that any HathiTrust seq anchor (seq = printed page + 2) lands on the named page, and the live state of any eHistory page. The tool-limited files are in C:/Users/mlege/gettysburg-map/tmp/sources-v2/v2nd2/ (my cache only; no tracked files touched).
systemic_findings: HathiTrust is bot-blocked today: catalog.hathitrust.org/robots.txt returned a Cloudflare managed challenge (HTTP 403, 'Just a moment...') to an honest-UA request. I did not retry or work around it, and did not fetch babel.hathitrust.org. The identity of coo.31924077728255 (Cornell, ser.1:v.27:pt.2:Reports, 'pd / Full view') rests on the first run's stored catalog response (tmp/sources-v2/cache/http/1e/1e692b49..., fetched 2026-10-01T03:14Z), which I did not re-fetch. None of the HathiTrust seq anchors (printed page + 2 in all six reports) could be checked; they remain unverified.

The Wayback Machine holds 2021 captures of all four eHistory pages (Serial 045 = vol. 27 pt. 3, page = printed page). Each capture matches the IA scan page in header and text, confirming the URL shape and content as of 2021. This is not a live check, and eHistory itself was never requested.

The IA scans (warofrebellion272unit, warofrebellion273unit) are the reliable text source: US Government imprint 1889 per the title pages, IA 'public domain' statement, constant leaf = printed page + 6 at all ten pages I checked, and the BookReader n index = leaf - 1 (image-confirmed at n86 = p. 81, n218 = p. 213, n560 = p. 555). Non-access leaves are only the color card and last leaf, so OCR object k = BookReader n(k-1).

OCR quality caveat for the quote corpus: the IA scan itself clips the left margin on several pt. 2 pages (visible on the p. 81 image; OCR lines lose 1-3 leading characters on pp. 83-84 and 459), and the right edge on p. 628. Numerals are unreliable: image-confirmed errors are 2,500 read as 8,500 (p. 555) and 3,750 read as 8,750 (p. 213). Any verbatim quote or number must be checked against the page image.

The one-line OR description template ('marches, positions, fighting and losses in the Gettysburg Campaign') is wrong or misleading for 4 of the 6 reports here (352 Winchester, 388 supplementary report by an officer not present in the fight, 496 no marches, 532 Aldie), and the template line does not match 868, a statistical table. Treat the template as a label, not a summary.
Dixon asterisks (Early No. 470 and Rodes No. 506) come from the Civil War Cycling index, which I fetched (robots.txt allows it); they match CWC's text. I did not check them against Dixon's book.

Comparison with the first pass: all 10 verdicts, rights tiers (A1), kinds (except 868) and relevance agree. Differences: I classed 868 as dispatch-or-order (letter tail plus its inclosure) where the first pass said compiled-volume-or-finding-aid; I report the eHistory links as not-fetched; and I added the clipped-margin and numeral-error caveats and the shared end page 564 for 460. No findings contradict the first pass.

Adams, First New York Cavalry, Third Brigade, of operations June 12-15.' dated 'Bloody Run, Pa., June 26, 1863', mid-page after Klunk's report. The report runs to p. 86, signed 'A. W. ADAMS, Major, Commanding Regiment' to Maj. John O. Cravens, A.A.G., and No. 399 (Alexander) begins on the same page. items.written: 1863-08-05 (49 days after the action of June 17)

Wickham. The text is the operations 'of the second, third, and fifth squadrons of this regiment, in the cavalry action near Aldie, on June 17'. He was told to 'assume command of the three squadrons present', and 'I was ordered to move my whole command up rapidly'. No. 579 (Rosser, also Aldie) starts on p. 747. Single page p. 746 matches the entry and the CWC index.

Quote from the image where the OCR shows noise. Commands three squadrons (second, third, fifth) in the fight, not the whole regiment.
issues: Aldie, June 17: an action of the cavalry screen before the invasion, not Gettysburg.

summary: All 10 entries in my batch (1, 37, 73, 109, 136, 172, 208, 244, 280, 316, all OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1) verified from the Internet Archive scan warofrebellion271unit, and I agree with all ten first-pass APPROVE verdicts and A1 tiers. For each one I viewed the scan image of the first page and read the report text in the IA OCR. Report number, rank, name, unit, first page and end page match the printed heading and the contents list. I did not read the middle ~5k characters of report 109 (the July 2-3 narrative), so its end-to-end text is only partly checked. The listed HathiTrust and eHistory links could not be checked: my robots.txt probes of babel.hathitrust.org, catalog.hathitrust.org and ehistory.osu.edu each returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' challenge, and I stopped there. Nothing from those three hosts was fetched or bypassed. The title page (viewed, n6) reads 'Washington: Government Printing Office, 1889', and the IA metadata says 'In public domain. Work published prior to 1923', so the tier is A1 (US Government work, pre-1931). Differences from the first pass: description accuracy is partly inaccurate for 1, 244 and 316 (generic template); entry 73's registry start page and scan URL are one page late; and the registry's scan 'leaf' field is wrong for 136-316 while 'reader' is right. Replacement scan URLs are given where I fetched the matching page image.
systemic_findings: Link access: my own robots.txt probes (1 request each, 2026-10-01 ~08:40Z) of babel.hathitrust.org, catalog.hathitrust.org and ehistory.osu.edu all returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare managed-challenge page ('Just a moment...'), even for /robots.txt. I made no further requests to those hosts and did not try to get around the challenge. All 20 listed links in this batch are therefore unverified (blocked-to-bots). I used the Internet Archive scan instead (archive.org robots.txt allows it).

The HathiTrust 'seq = printed page + 20' pattern (QC-REPORT finding 5.2, 'look computed, not looked up') has a benign explanation for this batch. The Civil War Cycling index page (civilwarcycling.com/index/gettysburg-officer-reports-1/, robots.txt allows, fetched 200) publishes the same babel.hathitrust.org links: for all 10 entries the seq value is identical to the list's (34, 301, 380, 455, 517, 585, 660, 732, 819, 898). The list copied them from that index rather than computing them. The IA scan also has a constant offset: at the 10 sampled pages from p. 14 to p. 878 (image viewed at each), reader index n = printed page + 17. A constant offset is normal for this volume and is not evidence of computation. Whether the HathiTrust pages open at the right page is still unconfirmed.

IA's own folio file warofrebellion271unit_page_numbers.json is wrong for the second half of the volume. It maps printed p. 497 to leaf 517 (reader n516), but the image at n516 is p. 499 and p. 497 is at n514. It runs +2 leaves too high from about p. 452 (p. 497, 565, 640, 712, 799 checked) and +4 at p. 878. For p. 14, 281, 360 and 435 it agrees with the images. The registry's or_locator.scan.leaf for entries 136, 172, 208, 244, 280 and 316 carries these wrong values (517, 585, 660, 732, 819, 900), while the 'reader' field (514, 582, 657, 729, 816, 895) is correct. The 'leaf' field is inconsistent with 'reader' (leaf should equal reader+1) and should not be used. The folio JSON is a weak second witness for the structural check.

Entry 73 (Whittier) has a start-page problem in the registry. The printed heading 'No. 73 / Report of Lieut. Edward N. Whittier' and the first 3 lines of text are at the bottom of p. 360 (viewed, n377). The registry has ocr_pages [361,362], first_page_to_use 361 and scan url .../page/n378/mode/1up, which opens p. 361 without the heading. The list (360-362) and the historian's reports.json (360-362) are right. Suggested fix: first_page_to_use 360, scan n377.

Entry 208's registry 'written' is null because the IA OCR reads the date as 'July 16, 1868'. The image (n657) reads July 16, 1863. Quote and date extraction must be checked against the page image: OCR defects seen include the year in 208, a garbled p. 567 in 172 (wavy printed lines, legible in the image), a garbled Butterfield letter on pp. 20-21 in 1, jumbled casualty and ammunition tables in 73, 136 and 316, and a dropped contents-list column (No. 316 etc. blank) in the front matter. IA's _djvu.txt is one stream with no page breaks, so reports must be located by their 'No. N.' headings.

The OR description template ('written by the officer in command, describing the unit's marches, positions, fighting and losses') is wrong or loose for part of this batch. Entry 1 is the General-in-Chief's annual-report excerpt (4 omitted-passage rows) plus four addenda letters by other authors dated Dec 1863 to Feb 1864. Entry 244 has no casualty figures. Entry 316 is an ordnance officer's ammunition-issue report with no fighting by its author. Entry 109 is two papers (a report and a flags letter). Five of ten authors command a regiment, battery or battalion, not a larger unit. All ten were written 6 to 135 days after the battle (37: 6 days, 136: 7, 73 and 208: 13, 109: 14, 280: 20, 244: 25, 172: 43, 316: 51, 1: 135), so 'contemporaneous' means after-action reports, not same-day accounts.

The Dixon flags in the list (** 'particularly vivid / excellent explanation') for entries 109 and 316 are confirmed as markings on the Civil War Cycling index, which attributes them to B. Y. Dixon, 'Learning the Battle of Gettysburg: A Guide to the Official Records'. I could not read Dixon's book, so the attribution is unverified. The flag is a third party's opinion, not part of the OR text.

The eHistory shape (serial 043, page = printed page) is consistent with the standard OR serial numbering (Serial 43 = vol. 27 pt. 1) from my own background knowledge, not from anything fetched in this run. The eHistory pages themselves could not be opened. The HathiTrust volume id coo.31924077699761 = 'ser.1:v.27:pt.1:Reports', Cornell, Full view, comes from the builder's cached catalog-API response (link-probe.json, fetched 2026-10-01 03:14Z, status 200). I did not re-fetch it because the host now challenges my client.

items.evidence: IA scan image n31 (viewed) is printed p. 14 and holds the end of the contents list (No. 354-378). Mid-page 'No. 1. Report of Maj. Gen. Henry W. Halleck, General-in-Chief, U. S. Army, including operations in Southeastern Virginia and West Virginia', dated 'Washington, D. C., November 15, 1863', 'a summary of military operations since my last annual report', then a row of asterisks. OCR text read in full: 'Reynolds moved up to that place on July 1', Meade took command June 28, a short account of July 1-3, and total Union loss 'Killed, 2,834; wounded, 13,709; missing, 6,643; total, 23,186' with the footnote 'But see revised statement, p. 187'. Four '* * * * * * *' rows mark passages the OR omits (pp. 14, 17, 17, 18). The report ends p. 18 with 'All of which is respectfully submitted. H. W. HALLECK'. Addenda Nos. 1-4 follow: Dix to Halleck (Dec 15, 1863, York River expedition), Halleck to Dix (Dec 20), Butterfield to Meade (Jan 23, 1864, Harper's Ferry), Meade to Butterfield (Feb 4, 1864). The p. 22 header precedes 'No. 2. Report of Brig. Gen. Hermann Haupt', so pp. 14-21 is exact. The contents-list line and the Civil War Cycling index (OR 27,1:14-21) match the title exactly. The listed Hathi seq=34 is the same link Civil War Cycling publishes. The listed HathiTrust and eHistory pages were not opened (blocked).
items.extraction_notes: Text path: IA warofrebellion271unit_djvu.txt (or the historian or27-ocr adapter, id or27-1:0001, 3,625 words). The OR itself omits passages (asterisk rows), so quotes must not be presented as the complete report. OCR is poor on pp. 20-21 (Butterfield letter garbled); check against the image before quoting. Footnotes ('See Butterfield to Meade, January 23, 1864, p. 20', 'But see revised statement, p. 187') are compiler notes. Registry reader n31 is correct (viewed).

The report also covers Southeastern Virginia (Dix's York River expedition) and West Virginia; the addenda (4 letters by other authors) are a post-hoc dispute dated Dec 1863 to Feb 1864.
The text is an excerpt: four asterisk rows mark omitted passages.

summary: Entries 1726, 1730, 1734, 1738, 1742 and 1746 do not exist in Gettysburg_Sources_v2. The .docx has 1,714 numbered entries; I read word/document.xml directly and the last is "1714. OR Vol. 27, Part 3, p. 1059". Under the list's own Part XIII mapping (n = printed page + 655; n 1714 = p. 1059, n 658 = p. 3), the six numbers are extrapolated pages 1071, 1075, 1079, 1083, 1087 and 1091. The document never lists them, and its own Part XIII note says "Pages after 1059 were not checked". So there is no listed title, link or description to verify, and I cannot approve entries that are not in the list. I verified the six pages themselves, independently, in the Internet Archive scan of OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 3 (item warofrebellion273unit): item metadata, page_numbers.json (leaf 1077 = printed 1071, 1081 = 1075, 1085 = 1079, 1089 = 1083, 1093 = 1087, 1097 = 1091), the full OCR text, and viewed page images for all six. I also viewed p. 1072, which the historian rows tied to p. 1071 actually sit on. All six pages are real, are within the last 33 pages of the volume's body (the OCR shows the body ending on p. 1092, followed by "Alternate designations" and the index), and are US Government 1889 print (tier A1). The six pages hold four kinds of material. p. 1071 is a map plate with no text. p. 1075 holds the last Confederate items: Aug. 4, 1863 (Lee to Stuart, Special Orders No. 190), an undated Lee letter to Pickett, and General Orders No. 5 of Jan. 13, 1864. pp. 1079, 1083 and 1087 are Union documents in an Appendix ("documents received too late for insertion in proper sequence") that starts on p. 1076. p. 1091 is the tail of Kemper's brigade itinerary plus a War Department circular. Compared with the first pass: the page facts agree on every point I checked. My verdict differs: I give NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW for all six (nothing exists to approve; a human should decide whether to extend Part XIII past p. 1059 and renumber), where the first pass gave APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY. If the owner extends the pointers, my evidence supports tier A1 for all six pages, with the side and description corrections below.
systemic_findings: Numbering: the six batch numbers are not in the list. Entry numbers run 1-1714; the last is '1714. OR Vol. 27, Part 3, p. 1059' (read straight from word/document.xml; no hyperlink to /045/1060 or later). The batch numbers equal printed page + 655 (1726 = p. 1071 ... 1746 = p. 1091), the pattern of the list's Part XIII (n 658 = p. 3, n 1714 = p. 1059). Whoever built this batch extrapolated past the end of the list. The registry builder should not receive verdicts for n > 1714.

The body of OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 3 does not end at p. 1059: in the IA OCR the Confederate correspondence continues to p. 1092, where the circular signature (H. L. Clay) is followed by 'ALTERNATE DESIGNATIONS OF ORGANIZATIONS MENTIONED IN THIS VOLUME' and the index. Pages 1060-1092 are unlisted.

Appendix, not Confederate: p. 1076 carries the heading 'APPENDIX. Embracing documents received too late for insertion in proper sequence', followed by 'UNION CORRESPONDENCE, ETC.' (Curtin to Parker, June 15). The Appendix's Union section (about pp. 1076-1090) therefore breaks the list's own side rule ('Pages 3-813 Union, 874 onward Confederate'). Extending Part XIII past p. 1059 by that rule would mislabel the Union pages (verified Union by image on pp. 1079, 1083, 1087; by OCR running head on pp. 1081, 1085, 1089).

The historian index has the same side error: historian-src/corpus/or27/dispatches.json labels all 44 rows on pp. 1076-1090 'confederate'. Row p1076.1 has the heading 'APPENDIX.' parsed as its signer (it holds the end of the Joint Resolutions). The p1071.1 and p1071.2 rows are page-assigned to 1071 but the text is on p. 1072 (verified by image), because p. 1071 is a plate and its number mark sits next to the p. 1072 header in the OCR. p1075 has two rows for four printed items (Special Orders No. 190 carries signer 'R. E. LEE' although it is signed W. H. Taylor 'by order of General Lee'). These are findings against our own ingestion, not against the list.

Rights: all six pages are tier A1 on the evidence I fetched. The IA OCR title page prints 'Series I - Volume XXVII - in three parts. Part III - Correspondence, etc. Washington: Government Printing Office 1889', prepared 'under the direction of the Secretary of War'. IA metadata: publisher 'Washington : Govt. Print Office', sponsor University of Illinois, no rights or licence field; date field '1880' is the series start (MARC 260 c '1880-'), not this volume's imprint. The OR text is quotable; the eHistory (OSU) transcription layer and HathiTrust viewer are other parties' layers, so quote from the IA scan, not from them.

Could not verify: (a) HathiTrust catalog API: my read-only request for https://catalog.hathitrust.org/robots.txt returned a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' challenge (HTTP 403); I did not retry or work around it, so the HathiTrust rights record (the historian manifest cites coo.31924077700262 for pt. 3) is unverified by me; (b) the eHistory links for these pages (a blocked host, never fetched); (c) what the p1075.1 historian row actually contains (I read counts, not passage text); (d) the hour of the July 2 Second Corps position report and when Gibbon took command of the corps.

What I fetched (all polite, read-only, honest UA Gettysburg-sources-QC/1.0, 1.5-2 s between requests, archive.org/robots.txt checked first: only /control/ and /report/ disallowed): archive.org/metadata/warofrebellion273unit, _page_numbers.json, _marc.xml, _djvu.txt (3,406,041 bytes), and page images n1076, n1077, n1080, n1084, n1088, n1092, n1096 via /download/<id>/page/nNNNN_wNNN.jpg. Cached under C:/Users/mlege/gettysburg-map/tmp/sources-v2/v2verify2/. No browser was launched. Leaf-to-page mapping: leaf = printed page + 6; image n-index = leaf - 1.

Comparison with the first pass: every page-level fact it reported (page 1071 a Weldon sketch plate; p. 1075 Lee-Stuart, SO 190, Lee-Pickett, GO 5; p. 1079 Murphy/Parker/Curtin June 19-20; p. 1083 Williams/Butterfield/Curtin June 28-29; p. 1087 Second Corps position report plus Curtin/Parker July 2; p. 1091 Kemper's itinerary tail and the July 22 circular; Union rows mislabelled confederate in dispatches.json) held up against the scan. I add that p. 1076 starts an Appendix, that all 44 rows on pp. 1076-1090 are mislabelled, and that p. 1071 is a plate whose two historian rows really sit on p. 1072. The one disagreement is the verdict: APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY approves entries that are not in the list, whereas NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW leaves the decision with a person (extend Part XIII to p. 1092 with corrected sides, or drop the batch).

items.written: Aug. 4, 1863 (Lee to Stuart; Special Orders No. 190); Lee to Pickett printed '[No date.]' in the OR; General Orders No. 5 dated Richmond, Jan. 13, 1864, publishing Joint Resolutions approved Jan. 8, 1864. The first three are contemporaneous with the Culpeper/Rapidan situation after the campaign; GO 5 is about six months later.
items.rights_basis: US Government publication, GPO 1889 (title page in the IA OCR); the page content is Confederate official correspondence reprinted in the OR. IA metadata carries no rights field; IA date field says 1880 (series start). The HathiTrust catalog API was not usable.
items.evidence: No entry 1730 exists (the docx ends at 1714, p. 1059; 1730 = p. 1075 only by the n = page + 655 pattern). I checked the page in the IA scan: page_numbers.json maps leaf 1081 to printed '1075'. I viewed the image (n1080) and read the OCR. The running head is 'CORRESPONDENCE, ETC.-CONFEDERATE. 1075'. Four items print on the page. (1) Hdqrs. Army of Northern Virginia, Aug. 4, 1863, Lee to Maj. Gen. J. E. B. Stuart: the corps of Longstreet and Hill 'will cross the Rapidan to-day' and the army will be concentrated south of the river. (2) Special Orders No. 190, Aug. 4, 1863: Brig. Gen. B. H. Robertson is relieved from duty with two cavalry regiments; signed W. H. Taylor, A.A.G., 'By order of General Lee'. (3) '[No date.]' Lee to Gen. George E. Pickett: 'You and your men have crowned yourselves with glory', followed by the suggestion that Pickett destroy copy and original of his report and substitute a casualty-only report. (4) General Orders No. 5, Richmond, Jan. 13, 1864, publishing the Confederate Congress's Joint Resolutions of thanks to Lee and his army (approved Jan. 8, 1864; the text runs onto p. 1076). All four are post-battle; the Pickett letter refers to a Gettysburg report, but the page gives no date for it.

items.written: July 2, 1863 (contemporaneous; the position report has no time of day; Curtin to Parker and Parker to Curtin also dated July 2, 1863)
items.rights_basis: US Government publication, GPO 1889 (printed title page in the IA OCR); Union correspondence reprinted in the OR. IA metadata has no rights field. The HathiTrust catalog API was not usable. The hand-drawn diagram is a scan of a printed figure in the same 1889 volume.
items.evidence: No entry 1742 exists (the docx ends at 1714, p. 1059; 1742 = p. 1087 only by the n = page + 655 pattern). IA page_numbers.json maps leaf 1093 to printed '1087'. I viewed the image (n1092) and read the OCR. The running head is 'CORRESPONDENCE, ETC.-UNION. 1087'. The page opens with 'Headquarters Second Corps, Near Gettysburg, July 2, 1863. Report of the position of Second Army Corps, General Gibbon commanding'. Text: right rests on the Taneytown road, the line runs left parallel to the Emmitsburg road for one-half mile. A printed diagram of brigade positions follows, labelled 1st Div. (Gen. Caldwell: Cross, Kelly and Zook, Brooke), 2d Div. (Gen. Harrow: Hall, Ward, Webb) and 3d Div. (Gen. Hays: Willard, Smyth, Carroll) with the batteries of Rorty, Brown, Cushing, Hazard and Woodruff. More text: 'Second Division has single line thrown 40 to 60 yards in front general line'; ammunition train one-half mile to the rear on the Taneytown road, other wagons at Westminster; ground practicable for artillery and infantry, 'No woods'. It is signed N. H. Davis, Assistant Inspector-General, U. S. Army. The page then prints two July 2 telegrams: Curtin (Harrisburg) to Gov. Parker of New Jersey ('How soon will you send forward more troops?') and Parker's reply from Trenton ('coming in slowly ... by companies'). So roughly half the page is a battlefield position report and half is Harrisburg and Trenton troop-raising correspondence.
items.extraction_notes: The text is extractable but the diagram is not: about 40 lines of OCR noise between the opening text and 'Second Division has single line ...' (stray characters, 'Ist DIV', '3° DIV'). OCR error seen: 'Ho woods' for 'No woods'. The diagram needs manual transcription from the image (n1092) if its content is wanted, and the brigade labels must be read from the image. The page does not state the hour; I did not verify when Gibbon took command of the corps on July 2.

items.written: Itinerary of Kemper's brigade covers June 15-July 24, 1863 and is signed by First Lt. Kinloch Nelson, ordnance officer, undated; it can have been written only on or after July 24, 1863, about three weeks after the battle. War Department circular dated Richmond, July 22, 1863, signed H. L. Clay, Lt. Col. and A.A.G.
items.rights_basis: US Government publication, GPO 1889 (printed title page in the IA OCR); Confederate documents reprinted in the OR. IA metadata has no rights field. The HathiTrust catalog API was not usable.
items.evidence: No entry 1746 exists (the docx ends at 1714, p. 1059; 1746 = p. 1091 only by the n = page + 655 pattern). IA page_numbers.json maps leaf 1097 to printed '1091'. I viewed the image (n1096) and read the OCR. The running head is 'CORRESPONDENCE, ETC.-CONFEDERATE. 1091'. The page opens mid-document with the second half of the 'Itinerary of Kemper's brigade, June 15-July 24, 1863'; the heading and the June 15-30 entries are on p. 1090 in the OCR. Entries: 'July 1.-Did not change camp. 2d.-Marched to within about 5 miles of Gettysburg. 3d.-Marched down to battle-field, fought, and returned to the same camp'; then the retreat via Monterey, Waterloo and Williamsport; July 9 the prisoners were turned over to Gen. Imboden; later marches to Bunker Hill, Chester Gap and Culpeper Court-House by July 24; signed Kinloch Nelson. Below it is a War Department circular, Richmond, July 22, 1863 (issuing 20 rounds of ammunition above cartridge-box capacity on the eve of an engagement will be discontinued; it continues onto p. 1092, where H. L. Clay signs). The Gettysburg content is a single line for July 3 and is an itinerary entry, not a narrative.
items.extraction_notes: OCR is clean apart from small slips ('11m, 12 th', '21th' for 24th, 'oiir'). The itinerary is split across pp. 1090 and 1091 and the circular across pp. 1091 and 1092, so extraction must work by document, not by page. Image: n1096.
